The retrieved context does **not** include `domains/DM/spec.md`, which is the authoritative table listing Order / Label / Type / Role / **Core** for each DM variable. I therefore cannot give you the complete, verified list of Core=Req variables for DM without reading that file.

**What the retrieved context does support:**

- **STUDYID, DOMAIN, USUBJID** are the "Required Identifiers," and they are explicitly exempted from the domain-prefix naming convention precisely because they serve as merge/join keys. The same section notes that "All Demographics (DM) domain variables other than DMDTC and DMDY" are also exceptions to the prefixing rule — i.e., DM variables are unprefixed. [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md — 4.2.2 Two-character Domain Identifier]
- **DOMAIN** (Label: Domain Abbreviation; Type: Char; Role: Identifier; **Core: Req**) appears in 59 SDTM domains — all except RELREC, RELSPEC, RELSUB, SUPPQUAL — which includes DM. [Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md — §一 通用变量: DOMAIN]
- Definition of the Core value: a **Req** (Required) variable "is any variable that is basic to the identification of a data record ... or is necessary to make the record meaningful. Required variables must always be included in the dataset and cannot be null for any record." [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md — 4.1.5 SDTM Core Designations]
- Conformance requires "Including all Required and Expected variables as columns in standard domains, and ensuring that all Required variables are populated." [Source: chapters/ch03_submitting_data.md — 3.2.2 Conformance]

**Important caveat on a rule that is often misapplied to DM:** the rule "The Identifier variables STUDYID, DOMAIN, USUBJID, and --SEQ are required in all domains" applies to **domains based on a general observation class** [Source: chapters/ch02_fundamentals.md — 2.5 The SDTM Standard Domain Models]. **To get the definitive list**, read `domains/DM/spec.md` and filter on Core = Req. I have deliberately not enumerated the remaining candidates (e.g., subject/site/arm/country-type variables) from memory, since their Core designations must be read from the DM specification table rather than inferred.

results.answer:
## Key Assumptions for Adverse Event Data Collection & Coding (SDTMIG v3.4, AE domain)

### 1. Scope of what belongs in AE

- The AE dataset contains clinical data describing "any untoward medical occurrence in a patient or clinical investigation subject administered a pharmaceutical product and which does not necessarily have to have a causal relationship with this treatment" (ICH E2A). In consultation with regulatory authorities, sponsors may extend or limit the scope of collection (e.g., collecting pre-treatment events related to trial conduct, not collecting events assessed as efficacy endpoints); the events included must be consistent with protocol requirements. Events may be captured either as free text or via a prespecified list of terms. [Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md -- item_1]
- Events of clinical interest defined by the protocol that are **not** considered AEs are reflected in CE instead; sponsors must ensure that all adverse events are recorded in the AE domain, and write-in events on a CE CRF should be treated with caution. [Source: domains/CE/assumptions.md -- item_1] [Source: domains/CE/assumptions.md -- item_3]

### 2. Description and coding (AE assumption 2)

| Variable | Rule |
|---|---|
| AETERM | Captures the **verbatim** term collected for the event; it is the **Topic** variable, is Required, and must have a value. |
| AEMODIFY | Permissible; include if the sponsor's procedure permits modification of a verbatim term for coding, populated per sponsor procedures. |
| AEDECOD | Preferred term derived by the sponsor from the coding dictionary; **Required** and must have a value. AETERM is expected to be coded with a standard dictionary such as MedDRA; the dictionary name and version must be provided via the external codelist element in Define-XML. |
| AEBODSYS | The system organ class (SOC) from the coding dictionary assigned by the sponsor; **may differ** from the primary SOC in the dictionary's standard hierarchy. Expected to be populated. |

[Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md -- item_2]

Corresponding metadata: AETERM (Char, Topic, Req), AEMODIFY (Char, Synonym Qualifier, Perm), AEDECOD (Char, Synonym Qualifier, Req, MedDRA), AEBODSYS (Char, Record Qualifier, Exp); the MedDRA hierarchy code variables AELLT/AELLTCD/AEPTCD/AEHLT/AEHLTCD/AEHLGT/AEHLGTCD/AEBDSYCD/AESOC/AESOCCD are Expected Variable Qualifiers coded to MedDRA. [Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- AE — Adverse Events (Events)]

### 3. Prespecified terms; presence vs. absence of events (AE assumption 4)

- AEPRESP = "Y" indicates the term in AETERM was **prespecified on the CRF** (Char, Variable Qualifier, Perm, CT **C66742** = No Yes Response). Solicitation of specific AEs can affect reporting frequency, so the fact an event was solicited may be of interest to reviewers. [Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md -- item_4] [Source: domains/AE/spec.md -- Controlled Terminology]
- If it matters which prespecified AEs were **not** reported, those data go into a Findings-class dataset such as **FA** (Findings About Events or Interventions), with one record per prespecified term; events that actually occurred also exist in AE with AEPRESP="Y". [Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md -- item_4]
- In studies mixing prespecified and free-text collection: AEPRESP="Y" for prespecified events, **null** for free-text events. AEPRESP is Permissible and may be omitted entirely if all AEs were free text. [Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md -- item_4]
- A "no adverse events" record in the sponsor's data management system must **not** be carried into the submission AE dataset — only records for AEs that actually occurred are included. [Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md -- item_4]
- Practical illustration: prespecified probing questions ("Did the following occur?") are represented in FA with FATESTCD="OCCUR" (including FASTAT="NOT DONE" when not asked), while only the "Y" responses generate AE records with AEPRESP="Y". [Source: domains/FA/examples.md -- Example 4]

### 4. Disallowed Events-class qualifiers (AE assumption 10)

- **--OCCUR, --STAT, and --REASND are not used in AE** — they are the only SDTM Events-class qualifiers absent from AE, because AE contains only records for events that actually occurred. Negative/missing responses to probing questions are handled per assumption 4b (i.e., in FA). [Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md -- item_10]

### 5. Seriousness, severity and other qualifiers (AE assumption 7)

- If seriousness categories are collected secondarily to a leading "Serious?" question, the category variables (e.g., AESCAN, AESCONG) may be null when the answer is "No"; when "Yes", **at least one** must be "Y" and others may be "N" or null per sponsor convention. If instead the CRF collects a response for each category (e.g., AESDTH, AESHOSP), all category variables are populated and **AESER is derived**. [Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md -- item_7]
- AESCAN ("Involves cancer") and AESOD ("Occurred with overdose") are **not** part of the ICH definition of a serious AE but remain available for studies conducted under pre-ICH-adoption guidelines. [Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md -- item_7]
- A collected free-text description for "Other Medically Important Serious Adverse Events" goes to **SUPPAE** using the standard QNAM **AEOSOSP** (see Section 8.4 and Appendix C1). [Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md -- item_7]
- When a standard toxicity scale is used (e.g., NCI **CTCAE**), **AETOXGR** is used instead of AESEV; normally only one of the two is populated, though both may be populated in some cases. The dictionary name/version must be provided via the external codelist element in Define-XML. [Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md -- item_7]
- The seriousness flags and AEPRESP/AECONTRT use codelist **C66742** (No Yes Response); AESEV uses **C66769** (Severity/Intensity Scale for Adverse Events); AEACN uses **C66767**; AEOUT uses **C66768**; AEACNDEV uses **C111110**; AELOC uses **C74456**. [Source: domains/AE/spec.md -- Controlled Terminology]

### 6. Domain structure / definition of an "event" (AE assumption 7e)

- Structure is **one record per adverse event per subject**; it is the **sponsor's responsibility to define an event**, and this definition may vary and is usually described in the protocol. Options include one record spanning the event start-to-finish, or a new record when severity/causality/seriousness changes or worsens (each such record then represents a different event). [Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md -- item_7]
- The submission structure may differ from the collection structure — e.g., data collected per visit but submitted as summary records "collapsed" to the highest severity/causality/seriousness and final outcome; alternatively, changes over time may be submitted in an FA-based dataset. [Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md -- item_7] [Source: domains/FA/examples.md -- Example 6]

### 7. Related conventions seen in examples

- Timing: AESTDTC/AEENDTC are Expected (ISO 8601 datetime or interval); relative timing variables such as AEENRF are used when an AE is "Continuing" at the end of the study reference period. Times as well as dates may be collected to compare AE timing to start of treatment. [Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- AE — Adverse Events (Events)] [Source: domains/AE/examples.md -- Example 1]
- With very sparse prespecified-only collection, AE may carry only the term, AEPRESP, AEBODSYS and a collection date (AEDTC), with RELREC optionally relating AE and FA records. [Source: domains/AE/examples.md -- Example 3]

*Note on related domains:* MH follows parallel coding rules (MHTERM topic/Required, MHMODIFY permissible, MHDECOD/MHBODSYS from the dictionary, with MHCAT/MHSCAT used for prespecified body systems), which is useful when aligning AE and MH coding conventions. [Source: domains/MH/assumptions.md -- item_2]

results.answer:
## Purpose of TV

The Trial Visits (TV) dataset is a **Trial Design** domain that describes the **protocol-defined planned schedule of subject encounters** at the healthcare facility where the study is conducted [Source: domains/TV/assumptions.md -- overview]. Visits are defined as "clinical encounters" and are described using the timing variables **VISIT, VISITNUM, and VISITDY** [Source: domains/TV/assumptions.md -- overview].

Key roles it plays:

- **Provides the planned schedule against which actual subject activity is compared.** TV (together with TD) "provide the planned scheduling of assessments to which a subject's actual visits and disease assessments can be compared" [Source: domains/TV/assumptions.md -- overview]. The companion special-purpose domain SV captures the timing of the visits a subject *actually* passed through, plus visits that did not occur, and explicitly refers back to TV as the dataset that "defines the planned visits for the trial" [Source: domains/SV/assumptions.md -- item_1].
- **Governs controlled values of visit variables in all collected-data domains.** For planned visits, the values of VISIT, VISITNUM, and VISITDY used in any domain "must be those defined in the Trial Visits (TV) dataset," and there must be a one-to-one relationship between VISIT and VISITNUM [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.4.5 Clinical Encounters and Visits].
- **Scope of "visit" is flexible.** A protocol-defined trial visit need not equal one physical visit — it may span multiple clinic visits (e.g., screening recorded under one VISIT/VISITNUM) or represent only part of an extended in-patient stay. Diary and other out-of-clinic collection times may be described as "visits" in TV if desired [Source: domains/TV/examples.md -- Trial Visits Issues].
- **Contingent visits** (data collection triggered by an event or disease milestone) may be included in TV with a rule describing the circumstances; because VISITNUM must be populated for all TV records, a contingent visit's VISITNUM may not be chronological [Source: domains/TV/examples.md -- Trial Visits Issues].

## Structure

The general structure is **"One Record per Planned Visit per Arm."** For many trials (especially blinded ones) the schedule is identical across arms, so the structure becomes "One Record per Planned Visit" and **ARMCD should be left blank** on all records. If visits differ by arm, **ARMCD and ARM must be populated on all records**; if only some visits differ, populate ARMCD/ARM on all records for clarity, even though this creates near-duplicate records [Source: domains/TV/assumptions.md -- item_1].

## Variables

The two TV-specific (Rule) variables are:

| Variable | Label | Type | Role | Core | CT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TVSTRL | Visit Start Rule | Char | Rule | Req | — |
| TVENRL | Visit End Rule | Char | Rule | Perm | — |

[Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- TV — Trial Visits (Trial Design)]

Additional variables evidenced in the retrieved TV content:

- **STUDYID, DOMAIN, VISITNUM, TVSTRL, TVENRL** — shown populated in the tv.xpt examples [Source: domains/TV/examples.md -- Example 1]
- **VISIT, VISITDY** — the timing variables used to describe visits in TV [Source: domains/TV/assumptions.md -- overview]; VISITDY is "in effect, a special case representation of TVSTRL" and is useful when all visits are scheduled relative to study day 1 (RFSTDTC) [Source: domains/TV/assumptions.md -- item_3]
- **ARMCD, ARM** — populated when the visit schedule differs by arm [Source: domains/TV/assumptions.md -- item_1]
- **TAETORD** — referenced as sometimes needed together with an element name to specify when a visit is to occur, when an arm repeats the same element [Source: domains/TV/examples.md -- Example 1]

*Caveat:* the full TV variable specification table (domains/TV/spec.md) was not part of the retrieved context, so Type/Role/Core attributes are confirmed above only for TVSTRL and TVENRL. Consult domains/TV/spec.md for the complete ordered variable list with all attributes.

## Rule-writing guidance (TVSTRL / TVENRL)

- **TVSTRL** describes *when the visit should occur* and should reflect the protocol wording [Source: domains/TV/assumptions.md -- item_3]. This differs from element start rules, which describe the moment an element is considered to start; because gaps normally exist between visits, it is usually unnecessary to define the transition moment between visits — though trials of hospitalized subjects that divide time into visits like elements may need a transition event [Source: domains/TV/examples.md -- Trial Visits Issues].
- Start rules are usually expressed **relative to the start or end of an element or epoch** (e.g., "1-2 hours before end of First Wash-out", "8 weeks after end of 2nd Treatment Epoch"); the visit need not occur *during* the referenced element [Source: domains/TV/examples.md -- Trial Visits Issues].
- **TVENRL** describes when the visit should end, expressed relative to the start/end of an element or epoch, or relative to the start of the visit [Source: domains/TV/examples.md -- Trial Visits Issues].
- Rules may be non-quantifiable, e.g., TVSTRL = "On the day of, but before, the start of the Treatment Epoch" [Source: domains/TV/examples.md -- Trial Visits Issues].
- **Ranges** may be used (e.g., "12-16 days after the start of 2nd Element"); these are distinct from analysis "windows" used to select data points for a visit [Source: domains/TV/examples.md -- Trial Visits Issues].

## Related domains

Same class (Trial Design): TA, TD, TE, TI, TM, TS — with TA linked because "visits reference arms," and SE linked as "planned visits vs actual subject elements" [Source: domains/TV/spec.md -- Related Domains].

## PE Domain — Structure, PETESTCD Role, and Whole-Exam Value

### 1. Dataset structure
The retrieved context does **not** contain the authoritative dataset-level metadata row for PE (the Dataset-level Metadata table in Chapter 3 is truncated before the Findings-class domains), so I cannot quote the normative structure statement (e.g., "one record per ... per subject") for pe.xpt. **[Source: chapters/ch03_submitting_data.md § 3.2.1 Dataset-level Metadata]**

What can be observed from the domain's own example is the record granularity in practice: each record represents one body system examined (with location/laterality qualifiers) at one visit for one subject, and separate records are used for each abnormality found within a body system (distinguished by PESPID, PELOC, PELAT). **[Source: domains/PE/examples.md -- Example 1]** For the definitive structure string, confirm against the SDTMIG v3.4 dataset-level metadata / Define-XML specification.

Note that PE is classified as a **Findings** domain. **[Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- PE — Physical Examination (Findings)]**

### 2. PETESTCD
- **Label:** Body System Examined Short Name
- **Type:** Char
- **Role:** Topic
- **Core:** Req
- **Controlled Terms:** none specified
- **Order:** 7

**CDISC Notes:** Short name of a part of the body examined in a physical examination. It can be used as a column name when converting a dataset from a vertical to a horizontal format. The value cannot be longer than 8 characters, cannot start with a number (e.g., "1TEST" is not valid), and cannot contain characters other than letters, numbers, or underscores. Examples: "HEAD", "ENT". **[Source: domains/PE/spec.md -- PETESTCD]**

As the Topic variable, PETESTCD carries the subject of the observation (the body system examined), while PEORRES/PESTRESC carry the result. **[Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- PE — Physical Examination (Findings)]**

### 3. Value when the entire physical examination is one record
- **PETESTCD = "PHYSEXAM"** **[Source: domains/PE/spec.md -- PETESTCD]**
- Correspondingly, **PETEST = "Physical Examination"** (PETEST: Body System Examined, Char, Synonym Qualifier, Req, max 40 characters). **[Source: domains/PE/spec.md -- PETEST]**

## LBTESTCD — Lab Test or Examination Short Name

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| **Domain** | LB — Laboratory Test Results (Findings class) |
| **Order** | 8 |
| **Label** | Lab Test or Examination Short Name |
| **Type** | Char |
| **Controlled Terms** | C65047 — *Laboratory Test Code* |
| **Role** | Topic |
| **Core** | Req (Required) |

[Source: domains/LB/spec.md -- LBTESTCD] [Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- LB — Laboratory Test Results (Findings)]

### Role

LBTESTCD is the **Topic** variable of the LB domain — i.e., it carries the focus of the observation (which lab test was performed). Because it is **Required**, it must be present and populated on every record. Its companion variable **LBTEST** (Lab Test or Examination Name, Char, Synonym Qualifier, Req, CT **C67154**) carries the corresponding long/verbatim test name, limited to 40 characters. [Source: domains/LB/spec.md -- LBTEST]

### Controlled terminology

- Codelist code **C65047** (Laboratory Test Code), located in `terminology/core/lb_part2.md`; it is referenced only by LB.LBTESTCD. [Source: domains/LB/spec.md -- Controlled Terminology] [Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- §三 CT 交叉引用: C65047]
- The paired name codelist is **C67154** (Laboratory Test Name) in `terminology/core/lb_part3.md`, used by LBTEST. [Source: domains/LB/spec.md -- Controlled Terminology] [Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- §三 CT 交叉引用: C67154]
- Note: CDISC publishes a **LOINC to LB Mapping Codetable** (at https://www.cdisc.org/standards/terminology/controlled-terminology) that can be used to identify the appropriate CDISC CT value for a test with a given LOINC code (LBLOINC). [Source: domains/LB/assumptions.md -- item_8]

### Naming constraints

Per the CDISC Notes for LBTESTCD [Source: domains/LB/spec.md -- LBTESTCD]:

1. It is the **short name** of the measurement, test, or examination described in LBTEST.
2. **Maximum 8 characters.**
3. **Cannot start with a number** (e.g., "1TEST" is invalid).
4. **Cannot contain characters other than letters, numbers, or underscores.**
5. It is designed so it can serve as a **column name** when transposing a dataset from vertical (normalized) to horizontal format.

Examples: `ALT`, `LDH` (with LBTEST values "Alanine Aminotransferase", "Lactate Dehydrogenase" respectively). [Source: domains/LB/spec.md -- LBTESTCD] [Source: domains/LB/spec.md -- LBTEST]

results.answer:
## EX (Exposure) Domain — Purpose

**Class:** Interventions [Source: domains/EX/spec.md -- Related Domains]

**What it captures:** EX represents protocol-specified study treatment administrations. Examples of treatments represented in EX include, but are not limited to, placebo, active comparators, and investigational products. Treatments that are **not** protocol-specified belong in CM (Concomitant/Prior Medications) or another Interventions domain as appropriate. [Source: domains/EX/assumptions.md -- item_1]

**Key structural/usage rules:**
- EX is generally recognized as a **derived** dataset, where EXDOSU reflects the protocol-specified unit per study treatment. Collected data points (e.g., number of tablets, total volume infused) plus additional inputs (randomization file, concentration, dosage strength, product accountability) are used to derive EX records. [Source: domains/EX/assumptions.md -- item_1]
- EX is **required for all studies that include protocol-specified study treatment**. Exposure records may be directly or indirectly determined; metadata must describe the derivation. Methods, from most to least direct: actual observation of administration by the investigator; automated dispensing device records; subject recall; product accountability data; derived from the protocol (and when a study is still masked such that protocol-specified doses cannot yet be expressed in the protocol-specified unit, EX is not expected to be populated). [Source: domains/EX/assumptions.md -- item_1]
- Structure: **1 record per constant-dosing interval per subject**. The sponsor defines the constant-dosing interval — any period describable by a known treatment at a consistent dose, frequency, infusion rate, etc. E.g., for once-weekly dosing over 6 weeks, EX may be a single record spanning the 6-week treatment phase (if per-dose information is not collected) or up to 6 records (1 per weekly administration, if each administration is monitored). [Source: domains/EX/assumptions.md -- item_1]
- Timing is captured by start/end date/time of each constant-dosing interval. VISITNUM may be added only when exposure occurs entirely within a clinical encounter (then VISIT/VISITDY also become permissible); it must not be used to signal "start visit"/"end visit" of a longer dosing interval, since EX captures timing of *exposure*, not dispensing. For point-in-time administrations where only one date/time is collected, EXSTDTC should be copied to EXENDTC. [Source: domains/EX/assumptions.md -- item_4; domains/EX/spec.md -- EXENDTC]
- **Relationship to EC:** Collected exposure data points are represented in the Exposure as Collected (EC) domain; where the EC↔EX record relationship can be described, it should be defined in RELREC, and EX derivations must be described in the Define-XML document. [Source: domains/EX/assumptions.md -- item_5; domains/EC/assumptions.md -- item_1]
- EX contains medications **received** only, so --MOOD generally would not be used, and the qualifiers --PRESP, --OCCUR, --STAT, and --REASND would generally not be used. Any Identifier, Timing, or Findings-class qualifiers may be added as needed. [Source: domains/EX/assumptions.md -- item_6]

## EXTRT — the Topic variable

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| Variable | EXTRT |
| Label | Name of Treatment |
| Type | Char |
| Role | Topic |
| Core | Req |
| Controlled Terms | — (none specified) |

[Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- EX — Exposure (Interventions)]

**Usage rules:**
- EXTRT captures the name of the **protocol-specified study treatment** and is the topic variable of the domain. It is a Required variable and must have a value. [Source: domains/EX/assumptions.md -- item_2]
- EXTRT must contain **only the treatment name** — no dosage, formulation, or other qualifying information. For example, "ASPIRIN 100MG TABLET" is *not* valid; it should be split as EXTRT = "ASPIRIN", EXDOSE = "100", EXDOSU = "mg", EXDOSFRM = "TABLET". [Source: domains/EX/assumptions.md -- item_2]
- Placebo doses are represented as EXTRT = "PLACEBO" with EXDOSE = "0" (indicating 0 mg of active ingredient taken/administered). [Source: domains/EX/assumptions.md -- item_2]
- As with other Interventions domains, the topic variable is --TRT (i.e., EXTRT for EX). [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.3.6]
- EXCAT/EXSCAT can be used to group EXTRT values (EXCAT is "Used to define a category of EXTRT values"). [Source: domains/EX/spec.md -- EXCAT]

[Source: domains/MH/spec.md -- MHTERM] [Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- MH — Medical History (Events)]

As the **Topic** variable of this Events-class domain, MHTERM is the subject of the observation — it captures either the verbatim term collected for the condition/event, or the prespecified term used to solicit whether any of a group of conditions/events occurred. It is Required and must always be populated. [Source: domains/MH/assumptions.md -- item_2]

MH is described as "an events domain that contains data that includes the subject's prior medical history at the start of the trial." [Source: domains/MH/assumptions.md -- overview]

---

## Assumptions Guiding MH Data Collection

### 1. Description and coding (Assumption 2)
- **MHMODIFY** (Perm) should be included if the sponsor's procedures permit modification of the verbatim term for coding; populate per sponsor procedure — null values permitted.
- **MHDECOD** is populated with the dictionary preferred term when MHTERM is coded to a standard dictionary; the sponsor must provide dictionary name and version via the external codelist element in Define-XML.
- **MHBODSYS** holds the system organ class (SOC) from the coding dictionary assigned by the sponsor; it may differ from the primary SOC in the dictionary's standard hierarchy. It is expected to be populated.
- If the CRF collects medical history by prespecified body systems *and* the sponsor also codes terms, then MHDECOD/MHBODSYS come from the dictionary, while **MHCAT/MHSCAT** carry the prespecified body systems.

[Source: domains/MH/assumptions.md -- item_2]

### 2. Categorization and grouping (Assumption 3)
- **MHCAT/MHSCAT**: sponsor-defined categorization, often prespecified on the CRF. MHBODSYS is derived from the coding system whereas MHCAT is effectively assigned when the investigator records the condition under a prespecified category, so the two may differ.
  - Do **not** group all MH records into one generic category (e.g., "General Medical History") since that duplicates the domain code; if no finer categorization exists, omit the variable. If "General Medical History" is used as an MHCAT value, other MHCAT values should also exist (e.g., "Allergy Medical History," "Reproductive Medical History").
- **MHGRPID**: links related records *within a subject* in MH (e.g., a group of syndromes related to one disease). It must not substitute for MHCAT/MHSCAT, which group data *across* subjects.

[Source: domains/MH/assumptions.md -- item_3]

### 3. Prespecified terms; presence or absence of events (Assumption 4)
Medical history is generally collected either as free text or from a prespecified list of terms. Because solicitation can affect reporting frequency, the fact that an event was solicited is of reviewer interest. **MHPRESP** and **MHOCCUR** (both CT C66742, No Yes Response) are used together:

| Situation | MHPRESP | MHOCCUR | MHSTAT |
|---|---|---|---|
| Spontaneously reported event occurred | | | |
| Pre-specified event occurred | Y | Y | |
| Pre-specified event did not occur | Y | N | |
| Pre-specified event has no response | Y | | NOT DONE |

- MHPRESP = "Y" indicates the term was prespecified; MHOCCUR = "Y"/"N" indicates whether the prespecified condition occurred.
- For free-text events, MHPRESP and MHOCCUR should be **null**; both are Permissible and may be omitted entirely if all events were free text.
- **MHSTAT** (CT C66789, Not Done) and **MHREASND** describe prespecified questions with no collected response; both are Permissible and may be omitted if all data were free text or all prespecified conditions had MHOCCUR responses.
- When free text is used, do **not** create a record to indicate "no medical history" for a subject or a prespecified body system category.

[Source: domains/MH/assumptions.md -- item_4] [Source: domains/MH/spec.md -- MHOCCUR] [Source: domains/MH/spec.md -- Controlled Terminology]

### 4. Timing variables (Assumption 5)
- Relative timing assessments such as "Ongoing"/"Active" are common. **MHENRF** is used when the assessment is coincident with the start of the subject's study reference period (DM.RFSTDTC); **MHENRTPT** with **MHENTPT** are used when "Ongoing" is relative to another date (e.g., the screening visit date). See Section 4.4.7, Use of Relative Timing Variables.
- Additional timing variables (e.g., MHSTRF) may be used when appropriate.

[Source: domains/MH/assumptions.md -- item_5]

---

## Illustration from the examples
- Example 1: MHENRTPT = "ONGOING"/"BEFORE" from the "Ongoing at Study Start" question; two start-date types for congestive heart failure produce two records distinguished by MHEVDTYP = "SYMPTOM ONSET" vs. "DIAGNOSIS", grouped with MHGRPID = "CHF". [Source: domains/MH/examples.md -- Example 1]
- Example 2: MHCAT set to the CRF module (GENERAL MEDICAL HISTORY, STROKE HISTORY, RISK FACTORS); MHPRESP/MHOCCUR populated only for prespecified terms, per Assumption 4. [Source: domains/MH/examples.md -- Example 2]
- Example 3: MHPRESP = "Y" for all solicited conditions; for the unasked asthma question MHOCCUR is null, MHSTAT = "NOT DONE", MHREASND = "FORGOT TO ASK". [Source: domains/MH/examples.md -- Example 3]

*Note: MHEVDTYP uses codelist C124301 (Medical History Event Date Type); individual term codes must be confirmed in the terminology file.* [Source: domains/MH/spec.md -- Controlled Terminology]

## SUPPQUAL — Purpose and Definition

**SUPPQUAL** (Supplemental Qualifiers) is the mechanism SDTM provides for representing **non-standard variables (NSVs)**. The SDTM does not allow the addition of new variables to a domain, so the Supplemental Qualifiers dataset model is used to capture NSVs and their association to parent records in general-observation class datasets (Events, Findings, Interventions), Demographics (DM), and Subject Visits (SV) [Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/assumptions.md]. 

- **Dataset name/structure:** `supp--.xpt`, "Supplemental Qualifiers for [domain name]" — Class **Relationship**; structure is **one record per supplemental qualifier per related parent domain record(s)**, Tabulation [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.4.1].
- **Naming:** There is a one-to-one correspondence between a domain dataset and its SUPP-- dataset. The single combined SUPPQUAL dataset option from SDTMIG v3.1 was **deprecated**; e.g., DM qualifiers go in `suppdm.xpt`, AE in `suppae.xpt`. For split domains, longer names such as SUPPFAMH / SUPPQS36 / SUPPFACM are used, with RDOMAIN holding the 2-character domain code [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.4.2; chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.1.7]. For associated-persons FA data where "SUPPAPFAMH" would be too long, the "SUPP" fragment is shortened to "SQ" (e.g., SQAPFAMH) [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.4.2].

## Variables (SUPP-- / SDTMIG v3.4)

| Variable | Label | Type | Role | Core | CT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| STUDYID | Study Identifier | Char | Identifier | Req | — |
| RDOMAIN | Related Domain Abbreviation | Char | Identifier | Req | (DOMAIN) |
| USUBJID | Unique Subject Identifier | Char | Identifier | Req | — |
| IDVAR | Identifying Variable | Char | Identifier | Exp | * |
| IDVARVAL | Identifying Variable Value | Char | Identifier | Exp | — |
| QNAM | Qualifier Variable Name | Char | Topic | Req | * |
| QLABEL | Qualifier Variable Label | Char | Synonym Qualifier | Req | — |
| QVAL | Data Value | Char | Result Qualifier | Req | — |
| QORIG | Origin | Char | Record Qualifier | Req | — |
| QEVAL | Evaluator | Char | Record Qualifier | Exp | (EVAL) |

[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.4.1]

QEVAL is associated with codelist **C78735** per the variable index [Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- SUPPQUAL]. The SDTM v2.0 model form of SUPP-- additionally includes APID, POOLID, and SPDEVID as Identifiers (13 variables total) [Source: model/06_relationship_datasets.md -- 6.2].

Key constraints:
- QNAM ≤ 8 characters, cannot start with a number, and may contain only letters, numbers, or underscores; QLABEL ≤ 40 characters [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.4.1].
- The combination STUDYID…QNAM (first 6 columns) must be unique for every record — no duplicate QNAM for the same IDVAR/IDVARVAL within USUBJID in a domain. Where two evaluators supply the same concept, use distinct QNAM values (e.g., AETRTEMI vs. AETRTEMA) so reviewers can merge/transpose without loss [Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/assumptions.md].
- Linkage is via STUDYID, RDOMAIN, USUBJID, IDVAR/IDVARVAL. **Exception:** for DM parent records, IDVAR and IDVARVAL are null because STUDYID + RDOMAIN + USUBJID uniquely identify the DM record (one record per USUBJID) [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- Key Rules].
- **QVAL must never be null** — records generated with null QVAL (e.g., from transposing missing source values) must be deleted before submission [Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/assumptions.md].
- QORIG indicates the origin of the value (e.g., "CRF", "Assigned", "Derived") per Section 4.1.8, Origin Metadata; QEVAL is used only for subjective results (e.g., "ADJUDICATION COMMITTEE", "SPONSOR") and is null for objectively collected or derived data [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.4.1; domains/SUPPQUAL/assumptions.md].
- Controlled terminology for common QNAM/QLABEL values is in **Appendix C1, Supplemental Qualifiers Name Codes**; additional QNAM values may be created as needed [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- Key Rules].

## When to Use Supplemental Qualifiers

1. **Whenever a sponsor-defined qualifier has no standard SDTM variable** — since new variables cannot be added to a domain, the NSV must go to SUPP-- [Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/assumptions.md].
2. **Attributions** — an interpretation or subjective classification of one or more observations by a specific evaluator (e.g., a flag indicating whether an observation was clinically significant). SUPP-- allows as many attributions as needed, and can hold both objective and subjective data [Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/assumptions.md].
3. **Secondary evaluations** — for observations with primary and secondary evaluations of specific qualifier variables, put the primary evaluation in the standard domain and the secondary in SUPP--. QNAM is formed by appending "1" to the standard variable name; if that name is already 8 characters, replace the last character with "1" (e.g., AERELNST → AERELNS1); increment for further attributions [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.5.4].
4. **Evaluator identification for Interventions/Events**, which lack --EVAL — QEVAL can describe the evaluator for any data item in SUPP--, though it is not required for objective data [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.5.4].

Example (suppae.xpt): AESOSP "Other Medically Important SAE" (QORIG = CRF) and AETRTEM "Treatment Emergent Flag" (QORIG = Derived, QEVAL = SPONSOR) linked to AE via IDVAR = AESEQ, IDVARVAL = 1 [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.4.3].

## When NOT to Use Supplemental Qualifiers

Data that represent **separate observations** should be treated as separate observations, not as supplemental qualifiers [Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/assumptions.md]. Specifically, do **not** submit as SUPP--:

- Subject-level objective data that fit in **Subject Characteristics (SC)** (e.g., national origin, twin type).
- **Findings interpretations** that belong as an additional test code and result — e.g., an ECG interpretation record with EGTESTCD = "INTP", sharing the same EGGRPID or EGREFID as the other records for that ECG.
- **Comments** related to a record or records in a parent dataset — these belong in the **CO** special-purpose domain, even if collected on the same CRF record.
- Data **not directly related** to records in a parent domain — these belong in a separate general-observation-class or special-purpose domain.

[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.4.4]

Also note that for long text, Section 4.5.3 (Text Strings that Exceed the Maximum Length) governs representation of values greater than 200 characters [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- Key Rules].

## Domains That Include EPOCH

EPOCH appears in **44 domains**: AE, AG, CE, CM, CP, CV, DA, DS, DV, EC, EG, EX, FA, FT, HO, IE, IS, LB, MB, MH, MI, MK, ML, MS, NV, OE, PC, PE, PP, PR, QS, RE, RP, RS, SC, SE, SR, SS, SU, TA, TR, TU, UR, VS. [Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md]

This spans the Interventions domains (AG, CM, EC, EX, ML, PR, SU), Events domains (AE, CE, DS, DV, HO, MH), the bulk of the Findings domains, the special-purpose domain SE, and the Trial Design domain TA (where the epoch is a defining element of the arm path rather than an observation timing attribute). [Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md] [Source: domains/TA/assumptions.md]

## Purpose

EPOCH records the **trial epoch (study-design period) with which an observation is associated** — e.g., "SCREENING", "TREATMENT", "FOLLOW-UP". [Source: domains/SR/spec.md] [Source: domains/FA/spec.md]

Which date/time it is anchored to depends on the observation class:

- **Findings class:** base EPOCH on **--DTC**, since that is the date/time of the test or, for tests on specimens, the date/time of specimen collection. A rare exception is an interval specimen collection spanning two epochs, where **--ENDTC** may be the more appropriate basis. [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.1.3.1]
- **Interventions/Events classes:** base EPOCH on **--STDTC**, the start of the intervention or event. [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.1.3.1]

Individual domain specs reflect this, e.g. LB/PC/PP/IS/CP: "Epoch associated with the start date/time of the observation, or the date/time of collection if start date/time is not collected"; EG/RE: "Epoch associated with the date/time at which the assessment was made". [Source: domains/LB/spec.md] [Source: domains/PC/spec.md] [Source: domains/EG/spec.md] [Source: domains/RE/spec.md]

## Key Usage Rules

1. **Do not impute EPOCH.** Assign values where possible on the basis of CRF instructions and structure, even when date/time was not collected with sufficient precision to derive the epoch. If the epoch cannot be determined, EPOCH must be null. Assignment methods may be documented in the Define-XML document. [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.1.3.1]
2. **Not applicable before study participation.** Because EPOCH is a study-design construct, it does not apply to interventions/events that started, or findings performed, before the subject's participation in the study; EPOCH should be null for such records. Note that participation includes screening, which generally precedes DM.RFSTDTC. [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.1.3.1]
3. **Epoch values must be unique per epoch.** EPOCH values used in datasets such as EX and DS must differ across epochs — e.g., in a 3-period crossover trial the three treatment epochs must each have a distinct name; they cannot all be "TREATMENT". [Source: domains/TA/assumptions.md]
4. **Placement limits.** As a Timing variable, EPOCH may be added to domains based on the 3 general observation classes; it may be added to special-purpose domains only where the SDTMIG domain assumptions specify it, and Timing variables cannot be added to SUPPQUAL datasets or to RELREC. [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.1.3]

results.answer:
## USUBJID as the cross-domain linking key

### 1. Definition and attributes

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| Label | Unique Subject Identifier |
| Type | Char |
| Role | Identifier |
| Core | Req (in most domains) |
| Controlled Terms | (none) |

The definition is deliberately identical across domains: "Identifier used to uniquely identify a subject across all studies for all applications or submissions involving the product." [Source: domains/DM/spec.md -- USUBJID] [Source: domains/VS/spec.md -- USUBJID] [Source: domains/CO/spec.md -- USUBJID]

### 2. Uniqueness scope is broader than a single study

The key point that makes USUBJID a linking key rather than just a within-study ID is that its uniqueness is defined **across all studies for all applications or submissions involving the product** — not merely within STUDYID. DM adds the construction guidance: "This must be a unique value, and could be a compound identifier formed by concatenating STUDYID-SITEID-SUBJID." [Source: domains/DM/spec.md -- USUBJID]

This means the same subject carries the same USUBJID value in every dataset of a study, and (for the same person) across studies in the submission, which allows integrated/pooled analysis datasets to be assembled by joining on USUBJID.

### 3. Near-universal presence in subject-level domains

USUBJID appears in 55 SDTM domains — all domains except OI, TA, TD, TE, TI, TM, TS, TV. [Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- §一 通用变量: USUBJID]

The exclusions are exactly the study-level/trial-design and study-reference datasets (trial design domains and Non-host Organism Identifiers), which describe the trial rather than individual subjects — so there is nothing to link to a subject. Consequently, every subject-level observation record in Interventions, Events, Findings, and Special-Purpose domains carries USUBJID, and DM acts as the demographic "anchor" record for each USUBJID value. [Source: domains/DM/spec.md -- USUBJID]

Position in the record: USUBJID is normally Order 3 (immediately after STUDYID and DOMAIN) in observation domains, e.g. DM, VS, CV, GF, UR, HO, CP, IS, MK, PP. [Source: domains/VS/spec.md -- USUBJID] [Source: domains/PP/spec.md -- USUBJID] [Source: domains/MK/spec.md -- USUBJID]

### 4. Role in relationship datasets

USUBJID is also the join column used by the relationship datasets, which is where its "linking key" function is most explicit:

- **SUPPQUAL / SUPP--**: USUBJID is Order 3, Core Req, and is defined as "the value of USUBJID in the parent record(s)" — i.e. it is part of the key (with RDOMAIN, IDVAR/IDVARVAL) that ties a supplemental qualifier back to the parent domain record. [Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/spec.md -- USUBJID]
- **RELSPEC**: USUBJID at Order 2, Core Req, identifying the subject whose specimens are being related. [Source: domains/RELSPEC/spec.md -- USUBJID]
- **RELSUB**: USUBJID at Order 2, but Core **Exp** rather than Req, with the note "Either USUBJID or POOLID must be populated" — because a related "subject" may be a pool rather than an individual. [Source: domains/RELSUB/spec.md -- USUBJID]

### 5. Practical implications

- Joining any two subject-level domains (e.g. AE ↔ CM, LB ↔ EX) is done on STUDYID + USUBJID, with domain-specific sequence/timing variables used to refine to the record level.
- Because USUBJID is Char with no controlled terminology, the sponsor must define and apply a consistent value-construction convention (e.g. the STUDYID-SITEID-SUBJID concatenation suggested in DM) uniformly in every domain; any inconsistency breaks all cross-domain joins. [Source: domains/DM/spec.md -- USUBJID]
- USUBJID alone is not a record-level key; for record-to-record relationships across domains, the relationship datasets (SUPP--, RELREC, RELSUB, RELSPEC) combine USUBJID with domain and identifier-variable references. [Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/spec.md -- USUBJID]

**Note on scope of this answer:** the retrieved context covers the variable definitions and the relationship-dataset usage of USUBJID. For the full normative rules on record-level linking mechanisms (RELREC key structures, IDVAR/IDVARVAL usage) see chapters/ch08_relationships.md and chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md, which were not part of the retrieved context here.

results.answer:
## Linking AE Records to CM Records with RELREC

### Principle

The RELREC special-purpose dataset describes relationships between records for a subject. A relationship is defined by **adding one record to RELREC for each record (or group of records) to be related**, and assigning a common relationship identifier in RELID. The value of RELID is sponsor-chosen but **must be identical for all related records within USUBJID**; a standard naming convention is recommended (e.g., all letters, all numbers, capitalized) [Source: domains/RELREC/assumptions.md -- overview].

RELREC should be used to represent **explicit relationships, such as concomitant medications taken as a result of an adverse event** — i.e., relationships that were actually collected (explicit references/checkboxes on the CRF, or by CRF design), not relationships inferred analytically [Source: domains/RELREC/assumptions.md -- overview; Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.1.1 --GRPID Example].

### Key variables used

Records expressing the relationship are specified with STUDYID, RDOMAIN (the domain code of the record in the relationship, e.g., "AE" or "CM"), and USUBJID, together with IDVAR and IDVARVAL:

- **IDVAR** = the name of the identifying variable in the referenced domain; **IDVARVAL** = its value.
- **Single records** are related using a unique-record identifier such as --SEQ (AESEQ, CMSEQ). --SEQ uniquely identifies a record for a given USUBJID within a domain and is required in all domains except DM.
- **Groups of records** are related using a grouping variable such as --GRPID (CMGRPID). Using --GRPID "can be a more efficient method of representing relationships in RELREC, such as when relating an adverse event (or events) to a group of concomitant medications taken to treat the adverse event(s)."
- **--REFID** (sponsor-defined or external identifier) is another candidate for IDVAR, though it is never required.
- **RELTYPE** is left null for peer-record relationships; it is used only for dataset-to-dataset (ONE/MANY) relationships [Source: domains/RELREC/assumptions.md -- overview].

### Example — one AE related to two concomitant medications

Two distinct collected relationships for USUBJID = "123456": the AE with 2 CM records (RELID=1), and the same AE with 2 LB records (RELID=2). Each relationship gets its own RELID; the AE record is repeated once per relationship.

**relrec.xpt**

| Row | STUDYID | RDOMAIN | USUBJID | IDVAR | IDVARVAL | RELTYPE | RELID |
|-----|---------|---------|---------|-------|----------|---------|-------|
| 1 | EFC1234 | AE | 123456 | AESEQ | 5 | | 1 |
| 2 | EFC1234 | CM | 123456 | CMSEQ | 11 | | 1 |
| 3 | EFC1234 | CM | 123456 | CMSEQ | 12 | | 1 |
| 4 | EFC1234 | AE | 123456 | AESEQ | 5 | | 2 |
| 5 | EFC1234 | LB | 123456 | LBSEQ | 47 | | 2 |
| 6 | EFC1234 | LB | 123456 | LBSEQ | 48 | | 2 |

[Source: domains/RELREC/examples.md -- Peer Record Examples; Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.2.2 RELREC Dataset Examples]

### Example — collapsing the CM records with CMGRPID

If the sponsor grouped the 2 concomitant medications in CM with CMGRPID (e.g., "COMBO 1"), the same relationship among 5 records is represented with 4 RELREC rows instead of 5, by using IDVAR="CMGRPID":

| Row | STUDYID | RDOMAIN | USUBJID | IDVAR | IDVARVAL | RELTYPE | RELID |
|-----|---------|---------|---------|-------|----------|---------|-------|
| 1 | EFC1234 | AE | 123456 | AESEQ | 5 | | 1 |
| 2 | EFC1234 | CM | 123456 | CMGRPID | COMBO1 | | 1 |
| 3 | EFC1234 | LB | 123456 | LBSEQ | 47 | | 1 |
| 4 | EFC1234 | LB | 123456 | LBSEQ | 48 | | 1 |

[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.2.2 RELREC Dataset Examples; Source: domains/RELREC/examples.md -- Peer Record Examples]

Note that CMGRPID groups records only **within a subject within a domain** — identical CMGRPID values in different subjects denote unrelated groupings [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.1.1 --GRPID Example].

### Related notes

- AE itself carries **AECONTRT** (Concomitant or Additional Trtmnt Given; Char, Record Qualifier, Perm, Controlled Terms C66742, values "Y"/"N") to flag that another treatment was given because of the event — this is a record-level flag, not a link; the actual record-to-record link requires RELREC [Source: domains/AE/spec.md -- AECONTRT].
- The CM spec cross-references AE as "adverse events treated by concomitant medication" [Source: domains/CM/spec.md -- Related Domains].
- RELREC is not needed to associate SUPP-- or CO records with their parent records, since those datasets already carry the parent's key identifiers [Source: domains/RELREC/assumptions.md -- overview].

results.answer:
## Linking TR and RS in the Oncology Multi-domain Model

The oncology data model deliberately splits the information across TU (identification), TR (measurements/assessments), and RS (response evaluation), and relies on the **`--LNKID` / `--LNKGRP` identifier variables plus a RELREC relationship** to reconnect the records. Existing ID variables (`--GRPID`, `--REFID`, `--SPID`) cannot be used for this purpose because the SDTM reserves them for other uses [Source: domains/TR/assumptions.md -- item_1], [Source: domains/TR/assumptions.md -- item_2].

### 1. TR ↔ RS (measurements → response assessment): `TRLNKGRP` / `RSLNKGRP`

- **`TRLNKGRP`** is used to relate records in the TR domain to a response assessment record in the RS domain. The organization of data across TR and RS **requires a RELREC relationship** to link the related data rows, and a **dataset-to-dataset link** is the most appropriate linking mechanism. The `--LNKGRP` variable holds the values that support that RELREC dataset-to-dataset relationship and provides a unique code for each response and its associated tumor/lesion measurements/assessments [Source: domains/TR/assumptions.md -- item_2].
- On the RS side, the corresponding variable is **`RSLNKGRP`**, which "is used to provide a link between the records in a findings domain (e.g., Tumor/Lesion Results, TR; Laboratory Test Results, LB) that contribute to a record in the RS domain. Records should exist in the RELREC dataset to support this relationship." [Source: domains/RS/assumptions.md -- item_4]
- Importantly, the linkage is not TR-specific: the domain in which the contributing data reside (e.g., LB for lab-based criteria) does not affect whether a RELREC link to the RS record is created [Source: domains/RS/assumptions.md -- item_4]. Source data must still be represented in the topic-based domain to which they pertain (e.g., a lab value scored for a response goes in LB) [Source: domains/RS/assumptions.md -- item_5].
- **`RSLNKID`** may alternatively be used to define a RELREC relationship when a response evaluation or clinical classification measure relates back to another source dataset (e.g., a tumor assessment in TR) [Source: domains/RS/assumptions.md -- item_4].

In the published RS examples, `RSLNKGRP` is populated only on the summarizing record (e.g., `RSTESTCD = "OVRLRESP"` with `RSLNKGRP = "A2"`, `"A3"`), while the component target/non-target response rows are left blank — illustrating that the link group ties the overall response to its supporting measurement set [Source: domains/RS/examples.md -- RS — Examples - Disease Response].

### 2. TU ↔ TR (lesion identification → lesion results): `TULNKID` / `TRLNKID`

- **`TRLNKID`** relates records in the TR domain to an identification record in the TU domain; again this requires a RELREC relationship, best implemented as a dataset-to-dataset link, with `--LNKID` providing a unique code for each identified tumor/lesion/location of interest [Source: domains/TR/assumptions.md -- item_1].
- **`TULNKID`** is the TU-side counterpart, providing the unique code for each identified tumor/lesion; its values are compound and may encode the assessor role, target vs. non-target status, a tracking number, and lesion-split information. "A RELREC relationship record can be created to describe the link, probably as a dataset-to-dataset link." [Source: domains/TU/assumptions.md -- item_2]
- TR deliberately omits anatomical location, because that would duplicate what TU carries — this multi-domain approach exists to reduce duplicated stored information, which is exactly why the link variables are needed [Source: domains/TR/assumptions.md -- overview].
- Example of the identifier pairing in practice: for a new unequivocal tumor, the TR record carries `TRLNKID = "NEW0"` with `TRTESTCD = "TUMSTATE"`, `TRORRES = "PRESENT"`, and the TU record populates `TULNKID` to link to the associated TR information [Source: domains/TU/assumptions.md -- item_6].

### 3. RS ↔ other Interventions domains: `CMLNKGRP` / `PRLNKGRP`

When best response, duration of response, or progression on prior/follow-up therapies is represented in RS, the RS record may be related and linked to record(s) in CM using **`CMLNKGRP`** and **`RSLNKGRP`**; the analogous link to PR (e.g., radiotherapy, surgery) uses **`PRLNKGRP`** [Source: domains/RS/assumptions.md -- item_6].

### Summary table

| Linkage direction | Identifier in source domain | Identifier in target domain | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| TU → TR (lesion ID → results) | `TULNKID` | `TRLNKID` | RELREC, dataset-to-dataset [Source: domains/TU/assumptions.md -- item_2], [Source: domains/TR/assumptions.md -- item_1] |
| TR → RS (measurements → response) | `TRLNKGRP` | `RSLNKGRP` | RELREC, dataset-to-dataset [Source: domains/TR/assumptions.md -- item_2], [Source: domains/RS/assumptions.md -- item_4] |
| Other findings (e.g., LB) → RS | `--LNKGRP` (e.g., `LBLNKGRP`) | `RSLNKGRP` | RELREC [Source: domains/RS/assumptions.md -- item_4] |
| RS → source dataset (record-level alternative) | — | `RSLNKID` | RELREC [Source: domains/RS/assumptions.md -- item_4] |
| RS → CM / PR | `CMLNKGRP` / `PRLNKGRP` | `RSLNKGRP` | RELREC [Source: domains/RS/assumptions.md -- item_6] |

### Variable attributes (TR domain)

| Variable | Label | Type | Role | Core | CT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TRLNKID | Link ID | Char | Identifier | Exp | — |
| TRLNKGRP | Link Group | Char | Identifier | Perm | — |

[Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- TR — Tumor/Lesion Results (Findings)]

## 1. What the FA Domain Is

**Findings About (FA)** is a **subtype of the Findings general observation class**, with structure **One Record per Finding**, used to record findings that are *about* an observation belonging to the Interventions or Events classes [Source: model/02_observation_classes.md -- 3.1.3 The Findings Observation Class].

It uses the standard Findings general observation-class variables **plus the `--OBJ` variable**, which is positioned immediately after `--TEST` in the qualifier order [Source: model/02_observation_classes.md -- 3.1.3 The Findings Observation Class].

Key structural rules:

- The presence of `--OBJ` is what *defines* a domain as a Findings About domain: "`--OBJ` cannot be added to a standard Findings domain. A domain is either a Findings domain or a Findings About domain... When the `--OBJ` variable is included in a domain, this identifies it as an FA domain, and the `--OBJ` variable must be populated for all records." [Source: chapters/ch02_fundamentals.md -- Findings About — Naming Findings About Domains (Reference Material)]
- Any Identifier, Timing, or Findings qualifier variables may be added to FA, **but these should generally not be used: `--BODSYS`, `--MODIFY`, `--SEV`, `--TOXGR`** [Source: domains/FA/assumptions.md -- item_6].

### When to use FA (three criteria)
1. Data/observations that have **different timing** from the associated event or intervention *as a whole* (e.g., severity of an individual symptom at a point in time; repeated assessments of intermittent symptoms; a summary such as maximum severity of headache after each dose) [Source: domains/FA/assumptions.md -- item_6].
2. An observation about an event/intervention that **requires more than one variable** for its representation, preventing it from being a supplemental qualifier [Source: domains/FA/assumptions.md -- item_6].
3. Data or information that **indicate the occurrence of prespecified AEs** [Source: domains/FA/assumptions.md -- item_6].

Assessments of *parts* of events ("snapshots or slices") go in FA and **may or may not have parent records**, depending on whether the overall event was also recorded [Source: domains/FA/assumptions.md -- item_6]. For choosing between Events/Interventions/Findings/Findings About, see the decision questions in [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.6.3 Guidelines for Differentiating Between Interventions, Events, Findings, and Findings About Events or Interventions] and [Source: domains/FA/assumptions.md -- item_2].

## 2. FAOBJ Specification

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| **Order** | 9 |
| **Label** | Object of the Observation |
| **Type** | Char |
| **Role** | Record Qualifier |
| **Core** | Req |
| **Controlled Terms** | (none) |

**CDISC Notes:** "Used to describe the object or focal point of the findings observation that is represented by `--TEST`. Examples: the term (e.g., 'Acne') describing a clinical sign or symptom that is being measured by a severity test; an event (e.g., 'VOMIT', where the volume of vomit is being measured by a VOLUME test)." [Source: domains/FA/spec.md -- FAOBJ]

**FAOBJ + FATESTCD jointly form the topic:** "`--OBJ` is unique to Findings About. In conjunction with FATESTCD, it describes what the topic of the observation is; therefore, both are required to be populated for every record. FATESTCD describes the measurement/evaluation and FAOBJ describes the event or intervention that the measurement/evaluation is about." [Source: model/02_observation_classes.md -- 3.1.3 The Findings Observation Class]

FATESTCD is Req with codelist **C101832**; FATEST is Req with codelist **C101833**; FAOBJ is Req with no codelist [Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- FA — Findings About Events or Interventions (Findings About)].

## 3. How FA Links to Parent Domains (AE, CM, etc.)

There are **three distinct linkage mechanisms**, and they are complementary:

### (a) FAOBJ — semantic pointer, not a key
FAOBJ names the event/intervention the finding is about. In practice it is populated with the parent's topic value — e.g., in FA Example 6 "The values in FAOBJ are the values from AEDECOD" for the associated AE records (FAOBJ=Nausea for AETERM "Morning queasiness"/AEDECOD "Nausea") [Source: domains/FA/examples.md -- Example 6].

**Critical limitation:** "The FAOBJ variable alone is **not sufficient** to establish a relationship, because an events or interventions dataset may have multiple records for the same topic (e.g., `--TERM` or `--DECOD`, `--TRT` or `--DECOD`)." [Source: domains/FA/assumptions.md -- item_5]

### (b) RELREC — the formal record/dataset linkage
"When data collection establishes a relationship between FA records and an events or interventions record, the relationship should be represented in RELREC." [Source: domains/FA/assumptions.md -- item_5]

Conversely, when no relationship was collected, no RELREC is created — in FA Example 4 (prespecified AEs), "No relationship was collected to link the FAAE record for the occurrence indicator test with the AE entries, so no RELREC was created"; instead the corresponding AE records carry AEPRESP="Y" [Source: domains/FA/examples.md -- Example 4]. This matches the documented AE↔FA association for prespecified AE findings [Source: domains/AE/spec.md -- Related Domains].

For a **dataset-level** RELREC (e.g., between CE and FACE), "RDOMAIN may contain up to 4 characters to effectively describe the relationship between the CE parent records and the FACE child records" [Source: chapters/ch02_fundamentals.md -- Findings About — Naming Findings About Domains (Reference Material)].

### (c) Sponsor identifiers (FASPID)
Example 6 uses FASPID to carry the parent AE identifier: "The values in FASPID are the AE identifiers from AESPID" [Source: domains/FA/examples.md -- Example 6].

## 4. Naming/Splitting FA by Parent Domain

FA data may be kept in a single FA dataset, split, or moved to a custom domain [Source: chapters/ch02_fundamentals.md -- Findings About — Naming Findings About Domains (Reference Material)]:

1. **Single FA domain**, differentiated by FACAT/FASCAT values.
2. **Split FA domain** (per §4.1.7): DOMAIN = "FA"; prefixed variables use "FA"; dataset names = domain + up to 2 characters indicating the **parent** domain, e.g. **FAAE**, **FACE** (Findings About Clinical Events), **FAMH** (Findings About Medical History) — this convention may be used even for a single unsplit FA dataset that has a parent domain. FASEQ must be unique within USUBJID **across all split datasets**. Supplemental qualifiers are managed at split-file level (suppface.xpt, suppfamh.xpt) with RDOMAIN = "FA".
3. **Separate custom domain**, with a sponsor-defined DOMAIN not beginning with FA (the published example being **SR**, Skin Response) — all FA rules still apply, and prefixed variables use the chosen 2-character code.

See also [Source: domains/FA/assumptions.md -- item_3] and [Source: domains/SR/spec.md -- Related Domains].

## 5. Naming FATESTCD Consistently With the Parent Domain

Some Events/Interventions variables (e.g., OCCUR, SEV, TOXGR) describe the event/intervention *as a whole*. "When FA is used to represent findings about a part of the event or intervention (i.e., the assessment has different timing from the event as a whole), the FATESTCD and FATEST values should be the same as the variable name and variable label in the corresponding event or intervention domain." [Source: domains/FA/assumptions.md -- item_4]

| FATESTCD | FATEST |
|---|---|
| OCCUR | Occurrence Indicator |
| SEV | Severity/Intensity |
| TOXGR | Toxicity Grade |

[Source: model/02_observation_classes.md -- 3.1.3 The Findings Observation Class]

Illustration (Example 6): AESEV holds the maximum severity over the whole event, while per-visit maximum severity slices are FATESTCD="SEV", FATEST="Severity/Intensity", FAOBJ="Nausea", FAORRES=MILD/MODERATE, with FACOLSRT="MAXIMUM" and FAEVINTX="SINCE LAST VISIT" [Source: domains/FA/examples.md -- Example 6].

Note: associations between certain findings about cardiovascular interventions/events and their response codelists are described in the CV codetable on the CDISC controlled terminology page [Source: domains/FA/assumptions.md -- item_4].

## 6. FA vs. Supplemental Qualifier

If the data item has its own timing separate from the event/intervention (Criterion 1), FA is indicated; if a RELMIDS relationship to a disease milestone is needed, "it can be represented in FA, but not as a supplemental qualifier to the parent record" [Source: chapters/ch02_fundamentals.md -- Findings About — Naming Findings About Domains (Reference Material)]. Data requiring more than one variable also cannot be a supplemental qualifier (Criterion 2) [Source: domains/FA/assumptions.md -- item_6].

results.answer:
## Overview

The Trial Design Model (TDM) provides a standardized representation of the *planned* conduct of a trial — the same information that ICH E3 study‑schema diagrams and schedule‑of‑assessment tables convey. Its purpose is to let reviewers "clearly and quickly grasp the design of a clinical trial," compare designs across trials, search a warehouse for design features, and "compare planned and actual treatments and visits for subjects" [Source: domains/TA/assumptions.md]. TA, TE, TV, and TI each cover a different axis of that plan, and they are linked by shared key variables. All four are of class **Trial Design**, together with TD, TM, and TS [Source: domains/TA/spec.md; domains/TI/spec.md; domains/TV/spec.md; domains/TE/spec.md].

---

## 1. TE — the building blocks (vocabulary of elements)

**Structure:** One record per planned Element [Source: model/05_study_level_data.md]

| # | Variable | Label | Type | Role |
|---|----------|-------|------|------|
| 1 | STUDYID | Study Identifier | Char | Identifier |
| 2 | DOMAIN | Domain Abbreviation | Char | Identifier |
| 3 | ETCD | Element Code | Char | Topic |
| 4 | ELEMENT | Description of Element | Char | Synonym Qualifier |
| 5 | TESTRL | Rule for Start of Element | Char | Rule |
| 6 | TEENRL | Rule for End of Element | Char | Rule |
| 7 | TEDUR | Planned Duration of Element | Char | Timing |

TE "describes the basic building blocks of a trial design — discrete periods of time during which a specific type of treatment or activity is planned" [Source: model/05_study_level_data.md]. It contains **the definitions of the elements that appear in the TA dataset**; an element may appear multiple times in TA (in multiple arms, multiple times within an arm, or both) but appears **only once in TE** — analogous to "unique CRF pages." E.g., the Example Trial 1 matrix has 9 study cells but only 5 unique elements, so TE has 5 records [Source: domains/TE/assumptions.md]. TE also supplies the operational start/end rules and planned duration, including for elements of variable length [Source: domains/TE/examples.md].

## 2. TA — how elements are assembled into arms and epochs

**Structure:** One record per planned Element per Arm [Source: model/05_study_level_data.md]

| # | Variable | Label | Type | Role |
|---|----------|-------|------|------|
| 1 | STUDYID | Study Identifier | Char | Identifier |
| 2 | DOMAIN | Domain Abbreviation | Char | Identifier |
| 3 | ARMCD | Planned Arm Code | Char | Topic |
| 4 | ARM | Description of Planned Arm | Char | Synonym Qualifier |
| 5 | TAETORD | Planned Order of Element within Arm | Num | Timing |
| 6 | ETCD | Element Code | Char | Record Qualifier |
| 7 | ELEMENT | Description of Element | Char | Synonym Qualifier |
| 8 | TABRANCH | Branch | Char | Rule |
| 9 | TATRANS | Transition Rule | Char | Rule |
| 10 | EPOCH | Epoch | Char | Timing |

"An arm is an ordered sequence of elements; the same element may occur more than once in a given arm," and TA carries rules for branching when a choice exists and for transitions that let a subject skip ahead rather than proceed linearly [Source: model/05_study_level_data.md]. Conceptually: the planned participation period is divided into **epochs**; each **arm** is a planned path through the entire trial; each arm × epoch intersection is a **study cell**, populated with element(s) [Source: domains/TA/assumptions.md].

**The TE↔TA join:** `ETCD` is the Topic variable in TE and a Record Qualifier in TA — this is the key that links each arm position back to its element definition [Source: model/05_study_level_data.md]. TA/TE cross‑references state it directly: "TE — arms use elements" and "TA — elements compose arms" [Source: domains/TA/spec.md; domains/TE/spec.md].

**Sequencing logic is split across the two domains** as a 3‑step transition process [Source: domains/TE/examples.md]:

| Step | Question | Answered by |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Should the subject leave the current element? | `TEENRL` (TE) |
| 2 | Which element comes next? | `TABRANCH` (TA) if there is a branch; otherwise `TATRANS` (TA) |
| 3 | (subsequent element entry) | governed with `TESTRL` (TE) / `TAETORD` ordering |

TA Example 3 shows this in practice: `TABRANCH` populated on two records per arm for two branch points (randomization at screening, plus response‑based assignment), with `EPOCH` labeling SCREENING / BLINDED TREATMENT / OPEN LABEL TREATMENT [Source: domains/TA/examples.md]. Note that element ≠ epoch: in a crossover trial, "treatment effect" derives from element (placebo, 5 mg, 10 mg) whereas "period effect" derives from epoch [Source: domains/TE/examples.md].

## 3. TV — the planned visit schedule laid over the arms

TV represents the planned schedule of visits, and it is arm‑aware: "arms define visit schedules" / "visits reference arms," so a visit schedule can differ by arm [Source: domains/TA/spec.md; domains/TV/spec.md]. In TDM terms, TA/TE answer *what treatment/activity periods are planned and in what order*, while TV answers *when subjects are seen and data are collected* — corresponding to the schedule‑of‑assessments table (as opposed to the study‑schema diagram) called for by ICH E3 §9.1 [Source: domains/TA/assumptions.md; model/05_study_level_data.md §5.1.4 "Planned schedules for activities and data collection"].

*(The retrieved context does not include the TV variable specification table, so I am not listing TV variables; consult domains/TV/spec.md for VISITNUM/VISIT and the TV start/end rule variables.)*

## 4. TI — eligibility criteria for entering the design

TI "contains all the inclusion and exclusion criteria for the trial, and thus provides information that may not be present in the subject‑level data on inclusion and exclusion criteria" [Source: domains/TI/assumptions.md]. It is one of the two "tabular synopses of parts of the study protocol" (with TS) that describe subject eligibility for trial participation [Source: domains/TI/assumptions.md; model/05_study_level_data.md §5.1.5]. `TIRL` was included in anticipation of a computer‑executable representation of criteria, but no such method was developed [Source: domains/TI/assumptions.md].

TI defines the *entry gate*: which subjects may be assigned to an arm at all. It is the trial‑level counterpart of the subject‑level IE domain, which "contains records only for inclusion and exclusion criteria that subjects did not meet" [Source: domains/TI/assumptions.md].

---

## How they fit together (data flow)

```
TI  →  eligibility gate: full protocol criteria (subject-level exceptions land in IE)
TE  →  defines each unique Element: ETCD/ELEMENT + TESTRL/TEENRL/TEDUR
        │  (ETCD)
        ▼
TA  →  assembles Elements into Arms (ARMCD/ARM) ordered by TAETORD,
       grouped into EPOCHs (= study cells), with TABRANCH / TATRANS logic
        │  (ARMCD)
        ▼
TV  →  planned Visit schedule, which may be arm-specific
```

* **Shared keys:** `STUDYID` throughout; `ETCD` links TE→TA; `ARMCD`/`ARM` link TA→TV.
* **Planned vs. actual:** these planned structures are the benchmark against which subject‑level data are compared — TV planned visits vs. SE actual subject elements [Source: domains/TV/spec.md], enabling the TDM goal of comparing "planned and actual treatments and visits for subjects" [Source: domains/TA/assumptions.md].
* **Reuse downstream:** "Many Trial Design domains define study‑specific terminology, and variables and variable values from these domains are used in subject‑level domains" — e.g., `ARM`/`ARMCD`, `ETCD`/`ELEMENT`, `EPOCH`, and `VISIT`/`VISITNUM` appear in DM, SE, SV, and observation domains [Source: model/05_study_level_data.md].
* **Design judgment:** the granularity of elements (and hence the TE/TA content) is a modeling decision driven by analysis needs — e.g., a titration can be modeled as several fixed‑dose weekly elements, as titration + constant‑dosing elements, or as a single element [Source: domains/TE/examples.md].

results.answer:
## CO — Comments Domain

### Definition and structure

CO is a **special-purpose domain** that contains free-text comments collected alongside other data: `co.xpt, Comments — Special Purpose. One record per comment per subject, Tabulation.` [Source: domains/CO/assumptions.md] The model states the structure as "One record per comment per subject (or per study)" and notes comments are normally supplied by a principal investigator but may come from other sources such as central reviewers; when collected, comments should be submitted in a single Comments domain [Source: model/03_special_purpose_domains.md].

Comments are generally **not** responses to specific questions; they usually consist of voluntary free-text or unsolicited observations, either related to data in one or more SDTM domains or collected on a separate CRF page dedicated to comments [Source: domains/CO/assumptions.md].

CO has 15 variables: STUDYID, DOMAIN, RDOMAIN, USUBJID, POOLID, SPDEVID, COSEQ, IDVAR, IDVARVAL, COREF, COVAL (Topic), COEVAL, COEVALID, CODTC, CODY [Source: model/03_special_purpose_domains.md].

Importantly, comments related to records in a parent dataset must **not** be submitted as supplemental qualifiers, even if collected in the same CRF record — they belong in CO [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md].

### The referencing mechanism

CO is structured similarly to the SUPP-- dataset: it uses the same set of keys — **STUDYID, RDOMAIN, USUBJID, IDVAR, IDVARVAL** — to identify related records. STUDYID, USUBJID, and DOMAIN (= "CO") must always be populated [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md].

**RDOMAIN**
- Order: 3; Label: Related Domain Abbreviation; Type: Char; Role: Record Qualifier; Core: **Perm**; Controlled Terms: **C66734** (SDTM Domain Abbreviation)
- CDISC Notes: "Two-character abbreviation for the domain of the parent record(s). Null for comments collected on a general comments or additional information CRF page." [Source: domains/CO/spec.md]
- The codelist link is given as SDTM Domain Abbreviation (C66734) for RDOMAIN [Source: domains/CO/spec.md]
- Note the role differs from the other relationship datasets: in RELREC and SUPPQUAL, RDOMAIN is an **Identifier** with Core **Req** [Source: domains/RELREC/spec.md] [Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/spec.md]. RDOMAIN appears in 3 domains: CO, RELREC, SUPPQUAL [Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md]

**IDVAR / IDVARVAL** (Order 8 and 9; Char; Record Qualifier) hold the *name* of the key variable of the parent record and its *value*, respectively [Source: model/03_special_purpose_domains.md]. The 2-character domain code is used as "a value in the RDOMAIN variable in relationship tables" [Source: chapters/ch02_fundamentals.md].

### Three levels of granularity

CO accommodates 3 sources of comments [Source: domains/CO/assumptions.md] [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md]:

| Case | RDOMAIN | IDVAR / IDVARVAL | CODTC |
|---|---|---|---|
| a. Comment unrelated to any domain or parent record (e.g., log-style general-comments page); relationship to the subject is conveyed by USUBJID alone | Null | Null | Populate if captured |
| b. Comment related to a domain but not to specific records | DOMAIN code of the parent domain | Null | Populate if captured |
| c. Comment related to a specific parent record or group of parent records | DOMAIN code of the parent record(s) | Key variable **name** and **value** of the parent record(s) | Null — the timing of the parent record(s) is inherited by the comment record |

### Grouping several parent records

As with SUPP-- and RELREC, **--GRPID** (or other grouping variables) can be used as the value of IDVAR to relate a comment to multiple parent records. The limitation is that a single comment can only be related to a group of records in **one** domain, because RDOMAIN can hold only 1 value; if a single comment relates to records in multiple domains, the comment may need to be repeated in CO [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md].

### Supporting variables

- **COREF** (Comment Reference) may hold additional information describing the relationship that cannot be represented by RDOMAIN/IDVAR/IDVARVAL, e.g., CRF page number or name [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md].
- Timing variables (e.g., VISITNUM, VISIT) may be added to CO; see CO assumption 5 for the complete list of permissible Identifier and Timing variables [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md].
- **COVAL** is the Topic variable. When the comment text exceeds 200 characters, the first 200 characters go in COVAL, the next 200 in COVAL1, and further text in COVALn as needed [Source: domains/CO/assumptions.md] [Source: model/03_special_purpose_domains.md].
- **COEVAL** (Evaluator) and **COEVALID** (Evaluator Identifier) are subject to controlled terminology: Evaluator (C78735) and Medical Evaluator Identifier (C96777) [Source: domains/CO/spec.md].
