results.answer:
## RFSTDTC/RFENDTC vs. RFXSTDTC/RFXENDTC

DM contains four pairs of reference-period variables (RFSTDTC/RFENDTC, RFXSTDTC/RFXENDTC, RFCSTDTC/RFCENDTC, RFICDTC/RFPENDTC), which exist "to accommodate distinct reference-period definitions"; there are instances when the values may be exactly the same, "particularly with RFSTDTC-RFENDTC and RFXSTDTC-RFXENDTC." [Source: domains/DM/assumptions.md -- item_10]

### RFSTDTC / RFENDTC — sponsor-defined reference period

| Attribute | RFSTDTC | RFENDTC |
|---|---|---|
| Label | Subject Reference Start Date/Time | Subject Reference End Date/Time |
| Type | DateTime | DateTime |
| Controlled Terms | ISO 8601 datetime or interval | ISO 8601 datetime or interval |
| Role | Record Qualifier | Record Qualifier |
| Core | Exp | Exp |

[Source: domains/DM/spec.md -- RFSTDTC] [Source: domains/DM/spec.md -- RFENDTC]

- This pair **is sponsor-defined**, but usually represents the date/time of first and last study exposure. Certain study designs define the start of the reference period differently — e.g., studies with a washout period before randomization, or a medical procedure required during screening (e.g., biopsy). In those cases RFSTDTC may be the enrollment date, which is prior to first dose; because study day values are calculated from RFSTDTC, study days would then not be based on the date of first dose. [Source: domains/DM/assumptions.md -- item_10]
- RFENDTC is usually equivalent to the date/time when the subject was determined to have ended the trial, and often equivalent to the date/time of last exposure to study treatment. It is **required for all randomized subjects; null for screen failures or unassigned subjects**. [Source: domains/DM/spec.md -- RFENDTC]
- RFSTDTC is the variable used to calculate study day (--DY) variables. [Source: domains/DM/assumptions.md -- item_9]
- This pair is also the "sponsor-defined reference period" referenced by the relative timing variables --STRF/--ENRF in the general observation classes (e.g., CESTRF, CEENRF, CMENRF, MHENRF, AGENRF; codelist C66728). [Source: domains/CE/spec.md -- CESTRF] [Source: domains/MH/spec.md -- MHENRF] [Source: domains/CM/spec.md -- CMENRF]

### RFXSTDTC / RFXENDTC — fixed exposure reference period

| Attribute | RFXSTDTC | RFXENDTC |
|---|---|---|
| Label | Date/Time of First Study Treatment | Date/Time of Last Study Treatment |
| Type | Char | Char |
| Controlled Terms | ISO 8601 datetime or interval | ISO 8601 datetime or interval |
| Role | Record Qualifier | Record Qualifier |
| Core | Exp | Exp |

[Source: domains/DM/spec.md -- RFXSTDTC] [Source: domains/DM/spec.md -- RFXENDTC]

- This pair "defines a consistent reference period for all interventional studies and **is not open to customization**." RFXSTDTC and RFXENDTC always represent the date/time of first and last study exposure, guaranteeing that a reviewer can always reference the first/last study exposure period even when RFSTDTC/RFENDTC are defined differently. [Source: domains/DM/assumptions.md -- item_10]
- Derivation: RFXSTDTC = earliest value of EXSTDTC; RFXENDTC = latest value of EXENDTC (or latest EXSTDTC if EXENDTC was not collected or is missing). [Source: domains/DM/spec.md -- RFXSTDTC] [Source: domains/DM/spec.md -- RFXENDTC]
- Relationship to SE: RFXSTDTC should be the same as SESTDTC for the first treatment element in SE; RFXENDTC may often be the same as SEENDTC for the last treatment element. [Source: domains/DM/assumptions.md -- item_10]

**Summary of the difference:** RFSTDTC/RFENDTC is a *flexible, sponsor-defined* period that drives study-day calculation and may start at something other than first dose (e.g., enrollment); RFXSTDTC/RFXENDTC is a *fixed, non-customizable* period that is always first/last exposure to protocol-specified treatment, derived from EX. They often duplicate each other, but not always.

## When RFSTDTC is null

RFSTDTC is usually defined as the date/time of first exposure to study drug. In such studies, when data are submitted for subjects who were never treated, RFSTDTC will be null — specifically: [Source: domains/DM/assumptions.md -- item_9]

- subjects ineligible for treatment, e.g., screen failures (ARMNRS = "SCREEN FAILURE");
- subjects enrolled but not assigned to an arm (ARMNRS = "NOT ASSIGNED");
- subjects randomized but not treated (ARMNRS = "NOT TREATED").

Note the design consideration: for studies where a substantial portion of subjects are not expected to be treated (non-interventional/observational studies, studies with a no-treatment arm, or studies with a delay between randomization and treatment), a different protocol milestone may be chosen as the starting point for study day variables (i.e., for RFSTDTC), rather than leaving it null. [Source: domains/DM/assumptions.md -- item_9] The spec for RFSTDTC also points to assumption 9 for detail on when RFSTDTC may be null. [Source: domains/DM/spec.md -- RFSTDTC]

Related note: although RFSTDTC, RFENDTC, RFXSTDTC, RFXENDTC (and the other RF*/DTHDTC/BRTHDTC variables) hold date/time values, they carry a **Record Qualifier** role in DM — they are not timing variables, because they are not intended for use in the general observation classes. [Source: domains/DM/assumptions.md -- item_7]

## Reference Range Variables in LB

### LBORNRLO / LBORNRHI — reference range in original units

**LBORNRLO**
- **Label:** Reference Range Lower Limit in Orig Unit
- **Type:** Char
- **Role:** Variable Qualifier
- **Core:** Exp
- **Controlled Terms:** None
- **CDISC Notes:** Lower end of reference range for continuous measurement in original units. Should be populated only for continuous results. [Source: domains/LB/spec.md -- LBORNRLO]

**LBORNRHI**
- **Label:** Reference Range Upper Limit in Orig Unit
- **Type:** Char
- **Role:** Variable Qualifier
- **Core:** Exp
- **Controlled Terms:** None
- **CDISC Notes:** Upper end of reference range for continuous measurement in original units. Should be populated only for continuous results. [Source: domains/LB/spec.md -- LBORNRHI]

Note these are **Char** because they parallel LBORRES (original result), whereas the standardized-unit counterparts are **Num**:
- **LBSTNRLO** (Reference Range Lower Limit-Std Units, Num, Exp) — lower end of range for LBSTRESC/LBSTRESN in standardized units; populate only for continuous results [Source: domains/LB/spec.md -- LBSTNRLO]
- **LBSTNRHI** (Reference Range Upper Limit-Std Units, Num, Exp) — upper end in standardized units; populate only for continuous results [Source: domains/LB/spec.md -- LBSTNRHI]

### Non-continuous (character/ordinal) results
For tests without continuous numeric results (e.g., urine protein by dipstick, urine color), the range is carried in **LBSTNRC** (Reference Range for Char Rslt-Std Units, Char, Perm) — e.g., "-1 to +1", "NEGATIVE TO TRACE" [Source: domains/LB/spec.md -- LBSTNRC]. LBSTNRC may hold either an ordinal character range (e.g., "NEGATIVE to TRACE") or a delimited set of values considered normal (e.g., "YELLOW", "AMBER"); in these cases **LBORNRLO, LBORNRHI, LBSTNRLO, and LBSTNRHI should be null** [Source: domains/LB/assumptions.md -- item_2].

### LBNRIND — Reference Range Indicator

- **Label:** Reference Range Indicator
- **Type:** Char
- **Role:** Variable Qualifier
- **Core:** Exp
- **Controlled Terms:** C78736 (Reference Range Indicator)
- **CDISC Notes:** Indicates where the value falls with respect to the reference range defined by LBORNRLO and LBORNRHI, LBSTNRLO and LBSTNRHI, or by LBSTNRC. Examples: "NORMAL", "ABNORMAL", "HIGH", "LOW". Sponsors should specify in the study metadata (Comments column in the Define-XML document) whether LBNRIND refers to the original or standard reference ranges and results. **LBNRIND is not used to indicate clinical significance.** [Source: domains/LB/spec.md -- LBNRIND]

**Codelist C78736 (Reference Range Indicator, Extensible: Yes)** values as retrieved: ABNORMAL (C78802), HIGH (C78800), LOW (C78801), NORMAL (C78727) [Source: terminology/core/general_part4.md -- Reference Range Indicator]. The same codelist is used by CP.CPNRIND, IS.ISNRIND, MS.MSNRIND, and OE.OENRIND [Source: terminology/core/general_part4.md -- Reference Range Indicator].

### What LBNRIND is *not* for
- **Toxicity:** if toxicity grading is available, use **LBTOX** and **LBTOXGR** [Source: domains/LB/assumptions.md -- item_3].
- **Clinical significance:** represented per Section 4.5.5 (Clinical Significance for Findings Observation Class Data), in **LBCLSIG** [Source: domains/LB/assumptions.md -- item_3]; see LB Example 1, where results evaluated by the investigator as not clinically significant are captured via LBCLSIG rather than LBNRIND [Source: domains/LB/examples.md -- Example 1].

### Key Implementation Assumption (multiple races)

- Multiple race responses are represented in DM plus **SUPPDM**, per Section 4.2.8.3 (Multiple Values for a Non-result Qualifier Variable). If multiple races are collected, RACE = "MULTIPLE" and the additional values go to SUPPDM; controlled terminology for RACE must be used in **both** DM and SUPPDM so values are consistent whether stored in a column or a row [Source: domains/DM/assumptions.md -- item_6].
- If multiple races were collected and one was designated primary, DM.RACE holds the primary race and the others go to SUPPDM [Source: domains/DM/assumptions.md -- item_6].
- For "Other, Specify" free text, follow Section 4.2.7.1; if the sponsor does not map the collected value per current FDA guidance, RACE = "OTHER". For subjects refusing or not knowing their race, RACE may be "UNKNOWN" [Source: domains/DM/assumptions.md -- item_6].
- Note that "MULTIPLE" is not among the values listed in the C74457 rows shown above; its code must be confirmed in the terminology file [Source: terminology/core/dm.md -- Race].
- The **Racec-Ethnicc Codetable** (on the CDISC terminology page) maps collected race values to published race Controlled Terminology (and likewise for ethnicity) [Source: domains/DM/assumptions.md -- item_6].
- Collected race subcategories (CDASH CRACE01–CRACE21, from the **RACEC** codelist) are submitted as SUPPDM.QVAL with QNAM = "CRACEn" and QLABEL = "Collected Race n" [Source: domains/DM/examples.md -- Example 6].

results.answer:
## QSCAT — identifying the instrument

**Definition**

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| Variable | QSCAT |
| Order | 9 |
| Label | Category of Question |
| Type | Char |
| Controlled Terms | C100129 (Category of Questionnaire) |
| Role | Grouping Qualifier |
| Core | **Req** |

QSCAT "is used to specify the questionnaire in which the question identified by QSTEST and QSTESTCD was included. Examples: 'ADAS-COG', 'MDS-UPDRS'." [Source: domains/QS/spec.md -- QSCAT] The codelist is *Category of Questionnaire* (C100129), linked from the domain's controlled-terminology cross references [Source: domains/QS/spec.md -- Controlled Terminology].

**QSCAT is the instrument name carrier for QRS data.** The name of a QRS instrument is described under the variable --CAT in the relevant QRS domain (i.e., FT, QS, RS), and may be either abbreviations or longer names — e.g., "ADAS-COG", "BPI SHORT FORM", and "APACHE II" are all --CAT values that are shortened instrument names. Sponsors should always reference CDISC Controlled Terminology; the QRS naming rules for --CAT, --TEST, and --TESTCD and the list of instruments with published CDISC/NCI-EVS terminology are maintained at the CDISC controlled terminology page. For --CAT terminology, three codelists apply across the QRS domains: Category of Clinical Classification, Category of Functional Test, and Category of Questionnaire [Source: domains/QS/assumptions.md -- item_1].

**Sub-structure within an instrument** is carried by QSSCAT (Subcategory for Question; Char, Grouping Qualifier, Perm), "a further categorization of the questions within the category," e.g., "MENTAL HEALTH", "DEPRESSION", "WORD RECALL" [Source: domains/QS/spec.md -- QSSCAT]. Note that --SCAT values are **not** part of CDISC Controlled Terminology; they are controlled instead by the QRS supplements in which they are used [Source: domains/QS/assumptions.md -- item_2].

### Instrument-specific handling built on QSCAT

1. **All questionnaires live in one domain, discriminated by QSCAT.** A single data structure serves many instrument types: "all questionnaire data are placed in the QS domain, with particular questionnaires identified by QSCAT" [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.6.2 Guidelines for Forming New Domains].

2. **Splitting by instrument.** A domain based on a general observation class may be split according to values in --CAT, and when split on --CAT, --CAT must not be null. Split dataset names may be up to 4 characters — the domain code plus up to 2 additional characters (e.g., **QS36** for SF-36). Constraints that preserve re-appendability: DOMAIN must remain "QS" across all split datasets; all domain-prefixed variables (e.g., --TESTCD) must use "QS" as the prefix; QSSEQ must be unique within USUBJID across *all* split datasets; permissible variables need not appear in every split dataset. Supplemental Qualifier datasets are split in parallel (e.g., SUPPQS36) while RDOMAIN stays "QS" [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.1.7 Splitting Domains].

3. **Instrument-level non-standard qualifiers via SUPPQS with IDVAR = QSCAT.** Attributes that apply to an entire instrument rather than to a single item are related at the QSCAT level: RDOMAIN = "QS", IDVAR = "QSCAT", IDVARVAL = the instrument (e.g., "BPI", "ADAS-COG"), QNAM = "QSLANG", QVAL = "FRENCH"/"GERMAN". The value then applies to all of that subject's records where QSCAT equals the IDVARVAL [Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/examples.md -- Example 2] [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.4.3 Examples]. (Caution from the splitting rules: when IDVAR is something other than --SEQ, ensure parent-record uniqueness across split datasets so children do not join to the wrong parent [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.1.7 Splitting Domains].)

## QSTESTCD / QSTEST — organizing question-level data

| Attribute | QSTESTCD | QSTEST |
|---|---|---|
| Order | 7 | 8 |
| Label | Question Short Name | Question Name |
| Type | Char | Char |
| Controlled Terms | (published per-questionnaire codelists) | (published per-questionnaire codelists) |
| Role | **Topic** | Synonym Qualifier |
| Core | Req | Req |

[Source: domains/QS/spec.md -- QSTESTCD] [Source: domains/QS/spec.md -- QSTEST]

- **QSTESTCD is the topic variable for QS** — it is what the observation is *about*, i.e., the individual item/question (or derived subscore) being reported. It is the short name for QSTEST and "can be used as a column name when converting the dataset from a vertical format to a horizontal format." Length ≤ 8 characters, cannot start with a number (e.g., "1TEST" is invalid), and cannot contain characters other than letters, numbers, or underscores. Examples: "ADCCMD01", "BPR0103" [Source: domains/QS/spec.md -- QSTESTCD].
- **QSTEST** is the verbatim question name, ≤ 40 characters, e.g., "BPR01 - Emotional Withdrawal" [Source: domains/QS/spec.md -- QSTEST].
- **Terminology is instrument-scoped:** controlled terminology for QSTESTCD and QSTEST "is published in separate codelists for each questionnaire" [Source: domains/QS/spec.md -- QSTESTCD] [Source: domains/QS/spec.md -- QSTEST], and "QRS --TESTCD/--TEST terminology codelists are listed separately by instrument name" [Source: domains/QS/assumptions.md -- item_1].

### How the pieces work together

QSCAT (Grouping Qualifier) says *which instrument*; QSSCAT optionally says *which section/domain within the instrument*; QSTESTCD (Topic) + QSTEST say *which item*. Because the QSTESTCD codelists are per-instrument and their naming embeds the instrument prefix (e.g., "ADCCMD01" for ADAS-COG, "BPR0103" for a BPRS item), items remain unambiguous even though many instruments coexist in one vertical dataset. Results are then carried in QSORRES → QSSTRESC/QSSTRESN, where "if question scores are derived from the original finding, then the standard format is the score"; when a sponsor applies a codelist for statistically meaningful standardized scores (e.g., SF-36), QSORRES holds the decode and QSSTRESC/QSSTRESN hold the standardized code values or scores [Source: domains/QS/spec.md -- QSSTRESC]. Record-level uniqueness is provided by QSSEQ [Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- QS — Questionnaires (Findings)].

Other instrument-relevant QS qualifiers include QSMETHOD (Method of Test or Examination; Perm; QRS Method, C158113), QSSTAT (Completion Status; Perm; C66789) with QSREASND, and the flags QSLOBXFL (Exp), QSBLFL, QSDRVFL (C66742) [Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- QS — Questionnaires (Findings)] [Source: domains/QS/spec.md -- Controlled Terminology].

Note that the same --CAT/--TESTCD pattern applies to the sibling QRS domains FT and RS [Source: domains/FT/assumptions.md -- item_1] [Source: domains/FT/assumptions.md -- item_2].

## QNAM — Qualifier Variable Name

**Variable attributes** [Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/spec.md]:

| Attribute | Value |

QNAM is the Topic variable of the SUPP-- dataset — it holds the short name of the non-standard variable (NSV) being added, "which is used as a column name in a domain view with data from the parent domain... This will often be the column name in the sponsor's operational dataset." [Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/spec.md] [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md]

### Character constraints

Per the CDISC Notes for QNAM [Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/spec.md] [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md]:

1. **Maximum length: 8 characters** — "The value in QNAM cannot be longer than 8 characters."
2. **Cannot start with a number** — e.g., "1TEST" is not a valid QNAM value.
3. **Allowed characters: letters, numbers, and underscores only** — "QNAM cannot contain characters other than letters, numbers, or underscores."

(These are effectively the rules for a valid SAS V5 variable name, since QNAM becomes a column name when SUPP-- is transposed/merged into a domain view.)

### Related rules that interact with the 8-character limit

- **Secondary evaluations / attributions:** QNAM is formed by appending "1" to the corresponding standard domain variable name; when that variable name is already 8 characters long, the last character is replaced with "1" (incremented for additional attributions). Example: AERELNST → **AERELNS1** [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md, §4.5.4].
- **Text >200 characters:** the first QNAM describes the NSV with no numeric suffix, and additional 200-character segments use a sequential 1-digit integer appended to the name; if the domain variable name is already 8 characters, replace the last character with a digit (e.g., AEACNOTH → AEACNOT1, AEACNOT2) [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md, §4.5.3.2].
- **Uniqueness:** the combined values of the first 6 columns (STUDYID…QNAM) must be unique for every record — there must not be multiple records for the same QNAM as it relates to IDVAR/IDVARVAL for a USUBJID in a domain. Where two evaluators supply the same concept, use distinct QNAM values (e.g., "AETRTEMI", "AETRTEMA") [Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/assumptions.md].
- **Controlled terminology:** In the SUPP-- table QNAM is flagged with an asterisk (*), i.e., it may be subject to controlled terminology; standard values for QNAM and QLABEL for the most common supplemental qualifiers are in Appendix C1, Supplemental Qualifiers Name Codes. Additional QNAM values may be created as needed, following the CDISC Notes guidelines [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md] [Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/assumptions.md].

### Companion constraint (for contrast)
**QLABEL** (the long name/label associated with QNAM) is limited to **40 characters** [Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/spec.md]; the 40-character truncation convention described for --TEST also applies to QLABEL [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md, §4.5.3.1].

The domain assumptions reinforce this: "The DV domain is an Events model for collected protocol deviations and not for derived protocol deviations that are more likely to be part of analysis." [Source: domains/DV/assumptions.md -- item_1]

Consistent with the Events class, DV may take any Identifier variables, Timing variables, or Events general observation-class qualifiers, though the following are generally not used: --PRESP, --OCCUR, --STAT, --REASND, --BODSYS, --LOC, --SEV, --SER, --ACN, --ACNOTH, --REL, --RELNST, --PATT, --OUT, --SCAN, --SCONG, --SDISAB, --SDTH, --SHOSP, --SLIFE, --SOD, --SMIE, --CONTRT, --TOXGR [Source: domains/DV/assumptions.md -- item_3].

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| **Order** | 7 |
| **Label** | Protocol Deviation Term |
| **Type** | Char |
| **Controlled Terms** | (none) |
| **Role** | Topic |
| **Core** | Req |

**CDISC Notes:** Verbatim name of the protocol deviation criterion. Example: "IVRS PROCESS DEVIATION - NO DOSE CALL PERFORMED". DVTERM values will map to the controlled terminology in DVDECOD (e.g., "TREATMENT DEVIATION") [Source: domains/DV/spec.md -- DVTERM].

### Related notes
- Per the general assumptions, for an Events domain the topic variable is **--TERM**, typically stored as verbatim text [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.3.6 Storing Topic Variables for General Domain Models].
- The standardized counterpart is **DVDECOD** (Protocol Deviation Coded Term, Char, Synonym Qualifier, Perm) — controlled terminology for the name of the protocol deviation, e.g., "SUBJECT NOT WITHDRAWN AS PER PROTOCOL", "SELECTION CRITERIA NOT MET", "EXCLUDED CONCOMITANT MEDICATION", "TREATMENT DEVIATION" [Source: domains/DV/spec.md -- DVDECOD]. In the example dataset, DVTERM holds free text while DVDECOD holds the controlled term [Source: domains/DV/examples.md -- Example 1].
- Note that DV is not used for entry-criteria violations; violated inclusion/exclusion criteria at screening belong in IE, whereas a criterion violated during the study (after first dose) may be reported in DV [Source: domains/DV/assumptions.md -- item_2].

results.answer:
## Observation Class

DS (Disposition) is an **Events**-class domain.

- Chapter 2 explicitly names Disposition (DS) among the Events general observation class examples: Events capture "planned protocol milestones and occurrences, conditions, or incidents independent of planned evaluations" — e.g., Adverse Events (AE), Disposition (DS), Medical History (MH) [Source: chapters/ch02_fundamentals.md -- 2.3 The General Observation Classes].
- The variable index also lists the domain as "DS — Disposition (Events)" [Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- DS — Disposition (Events)].
- Consistently, the domain assumptions state that "Any identifier variables, timing variables, or **Events general observation-class qualifiers** may be added to the DS domain," while listing qualifiers that would generally not be used: --PRESP, --OCCUR, --STAT, --REASND, --BODSYS, --LOC, --SEV, --SER, --ACN, --ACNOTH, --REL, --RELNST, --PATT, --OUT, --SCAN, --SCONG, --SDISAB, --SDTH, --SHOSP, --SLIFE, --SOD, --SMIE, --CONTRT, --TOXGR [Source: domains/DS/assumptions.md -- item_6].

## Structure

The formal one-line dataset structure statement is not contained in the retrieved context, so I cannot quote it verbatim. What the retrieved context does establish about how DS records are structured:

- Records are keyed by the standard Events identifiers: DSSEQ (Sequence Number, Num, Identifier, Req), with DSGRPID, DSREFID, DSSPID as Perm identifiers [Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- DS — Disposition (Events)].
- Each record represents one of three kinds of occurrence, differentiated by DSCAT (Category for Disposition Event, Char, Grouping Qualifier, Exp, CT C74558): "DISPOSITION EVENT", "PROTOCOL MILESTONE", or "OTHER EVENT"; DSSCAT (Perm, CT C170443) further categorizes DSCAT (e.g., "STUDY PARTICIPATION", "STUDY TREATMENT" when DSCAT = "DISPOSITION EVENT") [Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- DS — Disposition (Events)] [Source: domains/DS/spec.md -- DSSCAT] [Source: domains/DS/assumptions.md -- item_3].
- Records are **point-in-time events, not intervals**: "Events represented in the DS domain do not have end dates; disposition events do not span an interval, but rather occur at a single date/time (e.g., randomization date, disposition of study participation or study treatment)." Hence the timing variables are DSSTDTC (Exp)/DSSTDY (Exp) for the event itself and DSDTC (Perm)/DSDY (Perm) for collection; EPOCH may be included and in DS is based on DSSTDTC, with values drawn from Trial Arms (TA) [Source: domains/DS/assumptions.md -- item_4] [Source: domains/DS/spec.md -- DSSTDTC] [Source: domains/DS/spec.md -- DSDTC].

## Role of DSTERM

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| Order | 8 |
| Label | Reported Term for the Disposition Event |
| Type | Char |
| **Role** | **Topic** |
| Core | Req |
| Controlled Terms | (none) |

[Source: domains/DS/spec.md -- DSTERM] [Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- DS — Disposition (Events)]

DSTERM is the **topic variable** of the domain — i.e., it specifies the focus of the observation, the role defined in the model as "specify the focus of the observation" [Source: model/01_concepts_and_terms.md -- 2.1 Model Concepts and Terms — Variables]. It holds the "Verbatim name of the event or protocol milestone. Some terms in DSTERM will match DSDECOD, but others, such as 'Subject moved', will map to controlled terminology in DSDECOD, such as 'LOST TO FOLLOW-UP'" [Source: domains/DS/spec.md -- DSTERM].

How DSTERM is populated depends on DSCAT [Source: domains/DS/assumptions.md -- item_3]:
- **DSCAT = "DISPOSITION EVENT"**: DSTERM contains either "COMPLETED" or specific verbatim text describing the reason for non-completion; DSDECOD is coded from the extensible codelist NCOMPLT (e.g., DSTERM = "Subject moved" → DSDECOD = "LOST TO FOLLOW-UP").
- **DSCAT = "PROTOCOL MILESTONE"**: DSTERM contains the verbatim (as collected) and/or standardized text; DSDECOD uses the extensible codelist PROTMLST.
- **DSCAT = "OTHER EVENT"**: DSTERM and DSDECOD use sponsor terminology; if a reason was collected it goes in DSTERM (e.g., DSTERM = "INVESTIGATOR ERROR", DSDECOD = "TREATMENT UNBLINDED"); if no reason was collected, DSTERM is populated with the value in DSDECOD.

DSTERM is qualified by DSDECOD (Standardized Disposition Term, Char, **Synonym Qualifier**, Req; CT C66727 / C114118 / C150811 — NCOMPLT for disposition events, PROTMLST for protocol milestones, OTHEVENT for other events) [Source: domains/DS/spec.md -- DSDECOD]. Of these codelist codes, C150811 is confirmed in the terminology file as "Other Disposition Event Response," extensible, used by DS.DSDECOD [Source: terminology/core/disposition.md -- Other Disposition Event Response].

results.answer:
## PR (Procedures) Domain — Purpose

PR captures procedures performed on/for a subject. It is built on the **Interventions** observation class [Source: domains/PR/assumptions.md]. Key scoping rules:

- The extent of physiological effect may range from observable to microscopic; **regardless of the extent of effect or whether it is collected in the study, all collected procedures are represented in this domain**. The protocol design should specify whether procedure information will be collected [Source: domains/PR/assumptions.md].
- **Measurements/results obtained from procedures are NOT placed in PR** — they go to their respective Findings domain(s). Example: a biopsy procedure is represented in PR, while the histopathology evaluation of the tissue sample goes to MI (Microscopic Findings). Whether the PR–MI relationship is described in RELREC depends on whether the relationship was collected (explicitly or implicitly) [Source: domains/PR/assumptions.md].
- Related pattern in oncology: when additional data are collected about a procedure used for tumor/lesion identification, the procedure data are stored in PR, and the link to the tumor/lesion identification record is recorded using RELREC [Source: domains/TU/assumptions.md].

Example procedure types in scope [Source: domains/PR/assumptions.md]:

| Type | Examples |
|---|---|
| Disease screening | mammogram, pap smear |
| Endoscopic examinations | arthroscopy, diagnostic/therapeutic colonoscopy, diagnostic/therapeutic laparoscopy |
| Diagnostic tests | amniocentesis, biopsy, catheterization, cutaneous oximetry, finger stick, fluorophotometry, imaging (DXA, CT, MRI), phlebotomy, pulmonary function test, skin test, stress test, tympanometry |
| Therapeutic procedures | ablation therapy, catheterization, cryotherapy, mechanical ventilation, phototherapy, radiation therapy, thermotherapy |
| Surgical procedures | curative/diagnostic/palliative/therapeutic/prophylactic surgery, resection, stenting, hysterectomy, tubal ligation, implantation |

## PRTRT — the Topic Variable

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| **Variable** | PRTRT |
| **Order** | 9 |
| **Label** | Reported Name of Procedure |
| **Type** | Char |
| **Controlled Terms** | (none) |
| **Role** | Topic |
| **Core** | **Req** (Required) |

**CDISC Notes:** Name of procedure performed, either preprinted or collected on a CRF [Source: domains/PR/spec.md].

Because PRTRT is Core = **Req**, it must always be present and populated in the PR dataset.

### Qualifiers that reference PRTRT
- **PRDECOD** (Standardized Procedure Name, Char, Synonym Qualifier, Perm, CT **C101858** = Procedure): standardized/dictionary-derived name of PRTRT. If the codelist "PROCEDUR" is not used, the sponsor is expected to provide the dictionary name and version in the external codelist element of the Define-XML document; if a term has no decode value, PRDECOD is null [Source: domains/PR/spec.md].
- **PRROUTE** (Route of Administration, Char, Variable Qualifier, Perm, CT **C66729**): route of administration for PRTRT [Source: domains/PR/spec.md].
- **PRDOSE** (Dose, Num, Record Qualifier, Perm): amount of PRTRT administered; not populated when PRDOSTXT is populated [Source: domains/PR/spec.md].
- **PRPRESP** (Pre-specified, Char, Variable Qualifier, Perm, CT **C66742**): used when a specific procedure is pre-specified on a CRF; values should be "Y" or null [Source: domains/PR/spec.md].

### Example of PRTRT population
Verbatim procedure names such as "Wisdom Teeth Extraction", "Reset Broken Arm", "Prostate Examination", "Endoscopy", "Heart Transplant" — here the sponsor chose to represent long verbatim text in mixed case (see Section 4.2.4, Text Case in Submitted Data) [Source: domains/PR/examples.md].

results.answer:
## TS — Trial Summary

### Purpose and structure

The TS dataset lets the sponsor submit a **summary of the trial in a structured, parameter/value format**. **Each record in TS contains the value of one parameter** — a characteristic of the trial (e.g., trial phase, protocol title, trial objectives), covering both planned and actual trial characteristics [Source: domains/TS/assumptions.md -- overview].

Key structural points:

- TS is a **trial-level (Trial Design) dataset** — it is not subject-oriented [Source: INDEX.md -- Trial Design Domains].
- A single parameter may appear on **multiple records**; e.g., a trial addressing both safety and efficacy has two records with TSPARMCD = "TTYPE", one with TSVAL = "SAFETY" and one with TSVAL = "EFFICACY". **TSSEQ differs for each record of the same parameter** — note this differs from subject-level datasets, where --SEQ is unique within subject [Source: domains/TS/assumptions.md -- item_12].
- TSVALCD is populated **only when controlled terminology exists for TSVAL**; e.g., for TSPARMCD = "PLANSUB" or "TITLE", TSVALCD is null [Source: domains/TS/assumptions.md -- item_9].

### Variables (as indexed)

| Variable | Label | Type | Role | Core | CT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TSSEQ | Sequence Number | Num | Identifier | Req | — |
| TSGRPID | Group ID | Char | Identifier | Perm | — |
| TSPARMCD | Trial Summary Parameter Short Name | Char | Topic | Req | C66738 |
| TSPARM | Trial Summary Parameter | Char | Synonym Qualifier | Req | C67152 |
| TSVAL | Parameter Value | Char | Result Qualifier | Exp | — |
| TSVALNF | Parameter Value Null Flavor | Char | Result Qualifier | Perm | ISO 21090 NullFlavor |
| TSVALCD | Parameter Value Code | Char | Result Qualifier | Exp | — |
| TSVCDREF | Name of the Reference Terminology | Char | Result Qualifier | Exp | C66788 |
| TSVCDVER | Version of the Reference Terminology | Char | Result Qualifier | Exp | — |

[Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- TS — Trial Summary (Trial Design)]

### TSPARMCD

- **Order:** 5
- **Label:** Trial Summary Parameter Short Name
- **Type:** Char
- **Role:** Topic
- **Core:** Req
- **Controlled Terms:** **C66738** — Trial Summary Parameter Test Code [Source: domains/TS/spec.md -- TSPARMCD; domains/TS/spec.md -- Controlled Terminology]
- **Length limit:** **limited to 8 characters**, with no special-character restrictions. Values should be short for ease of programming use, though TSPARMCD is not expected to serve as variable names. Examples: "AGEMIN", "AGEMAX" [Source: domains/TS/spec.md -- TSPARMCD].

Companion variable **TSPARM** (Trial Summary Parameter, codelist **C67152**, Trial Summary Parameter Test Name) carries the decoded term and **cannot exceed 40 characters** (e.g., "Planned Minimum Age of Subjects") [Source: domains/TS/spec.md -- TSPARM]. Controlled terminology for TSPARM is **extensible**; any added parameters must be explained in the TS dataset metadata [Source: domains/TS/assumptions.md -- item_6]. The value lists for TSPARM/TSPARMCD are maintained in CDISC Controlled Terminology [Source: domains/TS/assumptions.md -- item_5].

### Related terminology notes

- TSVAL holds the parameter value (e.g., "ASTHMA" when TSPARM = "Trial Indication"); it may be null only when TSVALNF is populated, and text over 200 characters continues into TSVAL1–TSVALn [Source: domains/TS/spec.md -- TSVAL].
- Parameter-to-response codelist associations for TSVAL are published in the **TS codetable**; recipients (e.g., US FDA Data Standards Catalog) may specify or override terminology for particular parameters [Source: domains/TS/assumptions.md -- item_8].
- TSVCDREF uses codelist **C66788** (Dictionary Name) [Source: domains/TS/spec.md -- Controlled Terminology].

Note: the retrieved excerpt of the TS specification lists variables from TSSEQ onward; the standard Identifier variables preceding it (Order 1–4) are not shown in the context provided.

results.answer:
## CE — Clinical Events

**Purpose / Scope**

The CE domain captures events of clinical interest that are **not** reported as adverse events. The determination of what is a clinical event versus an adverse event should be made carefully, with reference to regulatory guidance or in consultation with a regulatory review division; events of clinical interest defined by the protocol that are not considered AEs are reflected in CE [Source: domains/CE/assumptions.md -- item_1].

Typical CE content [Source: domains/CE/assumptions.md -- item_1]:
- Signs and symptoms of the disease under study (e.g., migraine headaches and associated signs/symptoms in a migraine treatment study, where migraines are not AEs per protocol).
- In vaccine trials, certain events treated as signs/symptoms rather than AEs. Note: if any such event is considered serious, then `--SER` and the SAE flags (`--SCAN`, `--SCONG`, `--SDISAB`, `--SDTH`, `--SHOSP`, `--SLIFE`, `--SOD`, `--SMIE`) would be required in the CE domain.
- Efficacy-endpoint occurrences (e.g., all occurrences of TIA, stroke, and death in an ischemic-stroke prevention study); related information may also appear in other datasets (e.g., the event leading to death also reported as reason for discontinuation in DS).

**Observation Class**

CE belongs to the **Events** general observation class, and therefore may use any variables from the Events class, including those found in the AE domain specification table [Source: domains/CE/assumptions.md -- item_6]; the class designation "CE — Clinical Events (Events)" is also given in the variable index [Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- CE — Clinical Events (Events)]. The Events class has the structure **One Record per Event** [Source: model/02_observation_classes.md -- 3.1.2 The Events Observation Class].

**CETERM**

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| Order | 8 |
| Label | Reported Term for the Clinical Event |
| Type | Char |
| Controlled Terms | (none) |
| Role | Topic |
| Core | Req |

CDISC Notes: "Term for the medical condition or event. Most likely preprinted on CRF." [Source: domains/CE/spec.md -- CETERM]

CETERM is the domain's **Topic** variable — the class-level counterpart is `--TERM` ("Reported Term", Char, Topic, "the collected name for an event observation") [Source: model/02_observation_classes.md -- 3.1.2 The Events Observation Class]. Related qualifiers of CETERM include `CEDECOD` (Dictionary-Derived Term, Synonym Qualifier) and `CEPRESP`, which indicates whether the event in CETERM was prespecified ("Y" for prespecified events, null for spontaneously reported events; CT **C66742** No Yes Response) [Source: domains/CE/spec.md -- CEPRESP; Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- CE — Clinical Events (Events)].

results.answer:
## PC — Pharmacokinetics Concentrations

### Purpose / Scope
PC is the Findings-class domain that captures **drug and metabolite concentration measurements as a function of time** in plasma or other specimens. The topic of PC is "plasma (or other specimen) drug concentration as a function of time" [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md — 8.6.2 Guidelines for Forming New Domains].

In addition to analyte concentrations, the domain **can be used to represent specimen properties (e.g., volume, pH)** [Source: domains/PC/assumptions.md — item_1].

PC is one of the two Pharmacokinetics domains, the companion being PP (Pharmacokinetics Parameters), which holds characteristics of the time-concentration curve (e.g., AUC, Cmax, Tmax, half-life, elimination rate constant). Two datasets are used because PK contains more than one topic, each with a different data structure [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md — 8.6.2; Source: domains/PC/spec.md — Related Domains].

### Dataset / Structure
- Dataset: **pc.xpt**, "Pharmacokinetics Concentrations — Findings"
- Structure: **One record per sample characteristic or time-point concentration per reference time point or per analyte per subject**; Purpose: Tabulation [Source: domains/PC/assumptions.md — overview]
- Equivalent phrasing in the domain-splitting discussion: "1 record per analyte per time point per reference time point (e.g., dosing event) per subject" [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md — 8.6.2]
- The **reference time point and the analyte are part of the natural key** for both PC and PP [Source: domains/PC/assumptions.md — §6.3.5.9.3].

### Key variables supporting this structure
| Variable | Label | Type | Role | Core |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PCTESTCD | Pharmacokinetic Test Short Name | Char | Topic | Req |
| PCTEST | Pharmacokinetic Test Name | Char | Synonym Qualifier | Req |
| PCORRES / PCSTRESC / PCSTRESN | Result variables | Char/Num | Result Qualifier | Exp |
| PCSPEC | Specimen Material Type | Char | Record Qualifier | Exp (CT C78734) |
| PCLLOQ | Lower Limit of Quantitation | Num | Variable Qualifier | Exp |
| PCDTC | Date/Time of Specimen Collection | Char | Timing | Exp |
| PCTPT / PCTPTNUM / PCELTM | Planned time point name/number/elapsed time | Char/Num | Timing | Perm |
| PCTPTREF / PCRFTDTC | Time Point Reference / Date-Time of Reference Point | Char | Timing | Perm |

[Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md — PC — Pharmacokinetics Concentrations (Findings)]

### Additional implementation notes
- Any Identifiers, Timing variables, or Findings general observation class qualifiers may be added to PC, but **--BODSYS and --SEV would not generally be used** [Source: domains/PC/assumptions.md — item_3].
- Sponsors must document which concentrations were used to calculate each parameter — either in analysis dataset metadata or via **RELREC** between PC and PP. When relating whole datasets, PCGRPID/PPGRPID serve as surrogate keys (RELTYPE = MANY on both sides) and must be populated so each analyte/reference-time-point combination has its own value. Four record-level linking methods are illustrated: A (many-to-many, PCGRPID/PPGRPID), B (one-to-many, PCSEQ/PPGRPID), C (many-to-one, PCGRPID/PPSEQ), D (one-to-one, PCSEQ/PPSEQ) [Source: domains/PC/assumptions.md — §6.3.5.9.3; Source: domains/PC/examples.md — Method D].

[Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- §一 通用变量: VISITNUM]

Note that VISIT and VISITDY appear in the same 36 domains [Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- §一 通用变量: VISIT] [Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- §一 通用变量: VISITDY].

### Related implementation rules

- For planned visits, values of VISIT, VISITNUM, and VISITDY must be those defined in the Trial Visits (TV) dataset, and there must be a **one-to-one relationship** between VISIT and VISITNUM. VISITNUM is numeric and used for sorting, with values matching planned chronological order wherever possible [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.4.5 Clinical Encounters and Visits].
- For unplanned visits, VISITNUM should generally still be populated (e.g., 99 for all unplanned visits, or fractional values such as 3.1), while VISITDY must **not** be populated [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.4.5 Clinical Encounters and Visits].
- Some domains not in the list above may add VISITNUM as an additional timing variable when data are visit-based. For example, in SU, if substance use information is collected more than once within the CRF, VISITNUM would be added, and VISITDY and VISIT would then be permissible [Source: domains/SU/assumptions.md -- item_4]. Similarly, in EX, VISITNUM may be added when exposure occurs entirely within a clinical encounter (e.g., an injection administered at the clinic), but it is **not** appropriate when a constant-dosing interval extends beyond the encounter (e.g., pills taken at home) [Source: domains/EX/assumptions.md -- item_4].
- General rule: all domains based on the 3 general observation classes should have at least 1 timing variable; in the Findings class, where data are usually collected at multiple visits, at least 1 timing variable must be used [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.4.5 Clinical Encounters and Visits].

[Source: terminology/core/general_part4.md -- No Yes Response]

**Usage notes**

- Y/N variables should normally be populated for **both** "Y" and "N" so that a blank is unambiguous; only where a single checkbox makes one response unambiguous (e.g., `--LOBXFL`) is it acceptable to populate only "Y" and leave the alternate blank [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.3.7 Use of "Yes" and "No" Values].
- Variables whose controlled terms are shown as "Y"/"N" may be extended to "U" or "NA" if the sponsor explicitly collects/derives Unknown or Not Applicable [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.3.7 Use of "Yes" and "No" Values].

## What `--STAT` indicates

`--STAT` is a Record Qualifier that flags **absence of data** for the record — i.e., that a prespecified question was not asked/not answered, or a measurement/test/exam was not done (in some Findings domains, also that a test was attempted but did not generate a result) [Source: domains/MS/spec.md] [Source: domains/CV/spec.md] [Source: domains/MB/spec.md].

Two conventional phrasings of the population rule appear across domains:

- "Should be null or have a value of 'NOT DONE'" — e.g., CMSTAT, AGSTAT, MSSTAT, CVSTAT, MBSTAT, BSSTAT [Source: domains/CM/spec.md] [Source: domains/AG/spec.md] [Source: domains/BS/spec.md]

The value cited in the CDISC Notes for codelist C66789 is **NOT DONE**; for the complete set of terms in C66789, consult the CDISC controlled terminology file [Source: domains/CM/spec.md].

This list reflects only the domains present in the retrieved context. `--STAT` with codelist C66789 is a cross-domain Record Qualifier used in many additional SDTMIG v3.4 domains (e.g., other Findings domains); to enumerate all of them, query VARIABLE_INDEX.md § CT cross-reference for C66789 [Source: knowledge_base/VARIABLE_INDEX.md].

results.answer:
## RELSUB Purpose and Structure

RELSUB is the Relationship-class dataset used to represent relationships **between persons who are both study subjects**. A relationship between a study subject and a person who is *not* a study subject may **not** be represented in RELSUB — that case may only be reported in APRELSUB. The existence of the RELSUB dataset should not drive whether relationships are collected; that remains a study-specific decision [Source: domains/RELSUB/assumptions.md -- item_1] [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- Assumptions].

Typical use cases: studies where pregnant women are treated and both mother and child(ren) are subjects, and studies of genetically based diseases where related subjects are enrolled [Source: domains/RELSUB/assumptions.md -- overview].

**Structure:** One record per relationship per subject [Source: model/06_relationship_datasets.md -- 6.4 Related Subjects (RELSUB)].

## Bidirectional Representation Rule

Every relationship between 2 study subjects is represented as **2 directional records**:

1. First subject's identifier in USUBJID, second subject's identifier in RSUBJID
2. Second subject's identifier in USUBJID, first subject's identifier in RSUBJID

The two SREL values describe the same relationship from each subject's viewpoint (e.g., "MOTHER, BIOLOGICAL" / "CHILD, BIOLOGICAL") [Source: domains/RELSUB/assumptions.md -- item_7] [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- Assumptions].

All collected relationships must be recorded. If 2 subjects have more than 1 relationship (e.g., a woman who is both maternal aunt and wet nurse to an infant), **each** relationship is represented by its own pair of 2 records [Source: domains/RELSUB/assumptions.md -- item_8].

## RSUBJID

- **Order:** 4
- **Label:** Related Subject or Pool Identifier
- **Type:** Char
- **Controlled Terms:** — (none)
- **Role:** Identifier
- **Core:** Req
- **CDISC Notes:** Identifier used to identify a related subject or pool of subjects. RSUBJID is populated with either the USUBJID of the related subject or the POOLID of the related pool [Source: domains/RELSUB/spec.md -- RSUBJID].

Additional rules governing RSUBJID and the subject identifiers:

- RSUBJID must be a USUBJID value present in the DM domain, and **must be populated in every record** [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- Assumptions].
- POOLID (Perm) was developed for nonclinical studies but may be used in human clinical trials if necessary; if POOLID is submitted, the POOLDEF dataset must also be submitted, and in any record exactly 1 of USUBJID and POOLID must be populated. If the study does not use POOLID, USUBJID must be populated in every record [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- Assumptions].

## SREL

SREL (Subject Relationship, Char, Record Qualifier, Req) carries codelist **C100130** (RELSUB) [Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- RELSUB — Related Subjects (Relationship)]. Values should be taken from the CDISC Controlled Terminology RELSUB codelist wherever possible; if no appropriate term exists, another term may be used, but the SREL term must not be **less specific** than the collected verbatim term (e.g., do not record "RELATIVE, FIRST DEGREE" when "brother" was collected) [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- Assumptions].

## Example (study HEM021 — dizygotic twins and their mother)

**dm.xpt:** HEM021-001 (mother, F), HEM021-002 and HEM021-003 (twin sons)

**relsub.xpt:**

| Row | STUDYID | USUBJID | RSUBJID | SREL |
|-----|---------|---------|---------|------|
| 1 | HEM021 | HEM021-001 | HEM021-002 | MOTHER, BIOLOGICAL |
| 2 | HEM021 | HEM021-001 | HEM021-003 | MOTHER, BIOLOGICAL |
| 3 | HEM021 | HEM021-002 | HEM021-001 | CHILD, BIOLOGICAL |
| 4 | HEM021 | HEM021-002 | HEM021-003 | TWIN, DIZYGOTIC |
| 5 | HEM021 | HEM021-003 | HEM021-001 | CHILD, BIOLOGICAL |
| 6 | HEM021 | HEM021-003 | HEM021-002 | TWIN, DIZYGOTIC |

Rows 1–2 give the mother→child direction; rows 3 and 5 the reciprocal child→mother direction; rows 4 and 6 the twin-to-twin relationship in both directions [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- Example].

results.answer:
## Why PC and PP are two separate domains

Pharmacokinetics is one of the scientific areas that SDTMIG explicitly cites as requiring **more than one data structure**, and therefore more than one dataset:

> "In other cases, a particular topic may be very broad and/or require more than 1 data structure (and therefore require more than 1 dataset). This implementation guide includes examples in microbiology and pharmacokinetics... These examples use 2 domain datasets because within these scientific areas there is more than 1 topic, and each topic results in a different data structure." [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.6.2 Guidelines for Forming New Domains]

The two topics/structures are:

| Domain | Topic | Structure |
|--------|-------|-----------|
| PC | Plasma (or other specimen) drug concentration as a function of time | One record per analyte per time point per reference time point (e.g., dosing event) per subject |
| PP | Characteristics of the time-concentration curve (e.g., AUC, Cmax, Tmax, half-life) and elimination rate constant | One record per parameter per analyte per reference time point per subject |

[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.6.2 Guidelines for Forming New Domains]

The PC domain specification states the structure as: "One record per sample characteristic or time-point concentration per reference time point or per analyte per subject, Tabulation" [Source: domains/PC/assumptions.md -- overview]

Both domains are in the **Findings** general observation class [Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- PC — Pharmacokinetics Concentrations (Findings)] [Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- PP — Pharmacokinetics Parameters (Findings)], and each lists the other as a **Shared Dataset** partner: PC → "PP — pharmacokinetic concentrations → parameters" [Source: domains/PC/spec.md -- Related Domains]; PP → "PC — pharmacokinetic parameters ← concentrations" [Source: domains/PP/spec.md -- Related Domains].

A further practical reason for the separation: PP is a **derived** dataset — "Pharmacokinetics Parameters is a derived dataset, and may be produced from an analysis dataset with a different structure. As a result, some sponsors may need to normalize their analysis dataset in order for it to fit into the SDTM-based PP domain." [Source: domains/PP/assumptions.md -- item_1]

## How they relate: documenting the derivation

Because PP results are computed *from* PC results, the linkage must be documented:

> "Sponsors must document the concentrations used to calculate each parameter. This may be done in analysis dataset metadata or by documenting relationships between records in the Pharmacokinetics Parameters (PP) and Pharmacokinetics Concentrations (PC) datasets in a RELREC dataset (see Section 8.2, Relating Peer Records, and Section 8.3, Relating Datasets)." [Source: domains/PC/assumptions.md -- item_3]

### Option 1 — Relating datasets (dataset-level RELREC)

If all time-point concentrations in PC are used to calculate all parameters for all subjects, the relationship can be expressed at the dataset level using `--GRPID` as the link, with USUBJID and IDVARVAL left null:

| Row | STUDYID | RDOMAIN | USUBJID | IDVAR | IDVARVAL | RELTYPE | RELID |
|-----|---------|---------|---------|-------|----------|---------|-------|
| 1 | ABC-123 | PC | | PCGRPID | | MANY | A |
| 2 | ABC-123 | PP | | PPGRPID | | MANY | A |

[Source: domains/PC/assumptions.md -- item_3]

Important caveat: "the reference time point and the analyte are part of the natural key... for both datasets. In this relationship, --GRPID is a surrogate key, and must be populated so that each combination of analyte and reference time point has a separate value of --GRPID." [Source: domains/PC/assumptions.md -- item_3]

### Option 2 — Relating records (record-level RELREC)

Four methods are illustrated, differing in which linking variables are used:

- **Method A** — many to many, using PCGRPID and PPGRPID
- **Method B** — one to many, using PCSEQ and PPGRPID
- **Method C** — many to one, using PCGRPID and PPSEQ
- **Method D** — one to one, using PCSEQ and PPSEQ

[Source: domains/PC/assumptions.md -- item_3]

The choice depends on whether subsets of concentrations were excluded from particular parameter calculations, since "the exclusion of some concentration values from the calculation of some parameters affects the values of PCGRPID and PPGRPID for the different situations" [Source: domains/PC/assumptions.md -- item_3]. Worked examples show, e.g., excluded PC records flagged with `PCGRPID = "EXCLUDE"` when time points are used for no parameters [Source: domains/PC/examples.md -- Method D (One to One, Using PCSEQ and PPSEQ)], and separate group IDs (`DY1_DRGX_A` / `DY1_DRGX_B` in PC, `DY1DRGX_A` / `DYDRGX_HALF` in PP) when some time points are excluded only from half-life calculations [Source: domains/PC/examples.md -- Method D (One to One, Using PCSEQ and PPSEQ)].

The decision logic is summarized as: "Do all parameters for each PK profile use all concentrations for all subjects? If so, create a PPGRPID value for all PP records and a PCGRPID value for all PC records for each profile for each subject, analyte, and reference time point. Decide whether to relate datasets or records. If choosing the latter, create records in RELREC for each PCGRPID value and each PPGRPID value (method A). Use RELID to show which PCGRPID and PPGRPID records are related. Consider RELREC methods B, C, and D as applicable." [Source: domains/PC/assumptions.md -- item_1]

### Option 3 — Linking via reference time point

An alternative shown in the PP examples is to populate the reference date/time so records align across domains: "Note that PPRFDTC is populated in order to link the PP records to the respective PC records." [Source: domains/PP/examples.md -- Example 1]
(Note: PC carries PCRFTDTC "Date/Time of Reference Point" and PP carries PPRFTDTC, Exp [Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- PC — Pharmacokinetics Concentrations (Findings)] [Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- PP — Pharmacokinetics Parameters (Findings)]; the example table uses the label PPRFDTC.)

## Structural echoes of the relationship in the variable sets

Both domains share the Findings backbone (`--TESTCD`/`--TEST`, `--ORRES`/`--ORRESU`, `--STRESC`/`--STRESN`/`--STRESU`, `--SPEC`, `--STAT`/`--REASND`) and both carry `--GRPID` (Char, Identifier, Perm) and `--TPTREF`/`--RFTDTC` timing variables, which is precisely what makes the RELREC linkage possible [Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- PC — Pharmacokinetics Concentrations (Findings)] [Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- PP — Pharmacokinetics Parameters (Findings)].

Differences reflect their distinct roles:
- PC has collection/assay-oriented variables such as PCNAM (Vendor Name, Exp), PCLLOQ (Exp) and PCULOQ, PCSPCCND, PCFAST, PCDRVFL, plus fine-grained time-point timing (PCTPT, PCTPTNUM, PCELTM, PCDTC Exp) [Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- PC — Pharmacokinetics Concentrations (Findings)].
- PP has derivation-oriented variables such as PPANMETH (Analysis Method, Perm, CT C172330), PPSTINT/PPENINT (planned assessment interval), and PPRFTDTC is Expected rather than Permissible; PPCAT is Expected (used to identify the analyte, e.g., "DRUG A PARENT" vs "DRUG A METABOLITE") [Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- PP — Pharmacokinetics Parameters (Findings)] [Source: domains/PP/examples.md -- Example 1].
- PP units use dedicated codelists whose choice depends on normalization: PKUNIT for non-normalized parameters; PKUDMG and PKUDUG when normalized by dose amount in mg or µg; PKUWG and PKUWKG when normalized by weight in g or kg [Source: domains/PP/assumptions.md -- item_3].

Finally, for PC: "Any Identifiers, Timing variables, or Findings general observation class qualifiers may be added to the PC domain, but the following Qualifiers would not generally be used: --BODSYS, --SEV." [Source: domains/PC/assumptions.md -- item_3]

results.answer:
## Naming of SUPP-- Datasets

There is a **one-to-one correspondence between a domain dataset and its Supplemental Qualifier dataset**. Each domain's non-standard variables (NSVs) are submitted in a separate dataset named `SUPP--`, where "--" is the source domain code [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.4.2 Submitting Supplemental Qualifiers in Separate Datasets].

| Parent domain | SUPP-- dataset |
|---|---|
| AE | `suppae.xpt` |
| CM | `suppcm.xpt` |
| DM | `suppdm.xpt` |

Separate Supplemental Qualifier datasets of the form `supp--.xpt` are **required** (e.g., `suppae.xpt`, `suppcm.xpt`) [Source: model/06_relationship_datasets.md -- 6.2 Supplemental Qualifiers (SUPP--)]; the single combined SUPPQUAL dataset option introduced in SDTMIG v3.1 was **deprecated** [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.4.2 Submitting Supplemental Qualifiers in Separate Datasets].

Special naming situations:

- **Split domains:** the SUPP-- name includes the additional 1–2 characters used to identify the split dataset (e.g., SUPPQS36, SUPPFACM), while **RDOMAIN still holds the 2-character domain code** (e.g., QS, FA). Longer names such as SUPPFAMH may be needed [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.1.7 Splitting Domains; chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.4.2].
- **Associated Persons:** when a name such as SUPPAPFAMH would be too long, and only in this case, the "SUPP" fragment is shortened to "SQ" (e.g., SQAPFAMH) [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.4.2 Submitting Supplemental Qualifiers in Separate Datasets].

The dataset label is "Supplemental Qualifiers for [domain name]", class **Relationship**, structure *one record per supplemental qualifier per related parent domain record(s)*, Purpose = Tabulation [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.4.1 Supplemental Qualifiers (SUPP--)].

## Variable That Identifies the Parent Domain

**RDOMAIN** — Related Domain Abbreviation; Char; Controlled Terms: (DOMAIN); Role: Identifier; Core: **Req**. It carries the two-character abbreviation for the domain of the parent record(s) [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.4.1 Supplemental Qualifiers (SUPP--); model/06_relationship_datasets.md -- 6.2 Supplemental Qualifiers (SUPP--)]. E.g., in `suppae.xpt`, RDOMAIN = "AE" [Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/examples.md -- Example 1].

## Full Linking Key

RDOMAIN alone identifies only the domain; the record-level link is made by the composite key:

- **STUDYID** (Req) — study identifier of the parent record(s)
- **RDOMAIN** (Req) — parent domain code
- **USUBJID** (Req) — value of USUBJID in the parent record(s)
- **IDVAR** (Exp) — the identifying variable in the parent dataset (e.g., --SEQ, --GRPID)
- **IDVARVAL** (Exp) — the value of that identifying variable in the parent record(s)

[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.4.1 Supplemental Qualifiers (SUPP--); domains/SUPPQUAL/assumptions.md -- overview]

Notes on the key:

- **DM exception:** for SUPP-- records related to DM, both IDVAR and IDVARVAL are null, because STUDYID + RDOMAIN + USUBJID uniquely identify the DM record (DM has one record per USUBJID) [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- Key Rules; domains/SUPPQUAL/assumptions.md -- overview].
- The combined values of the first 6 columns (STUDYID … QNAM) must be unique for every record; there must not be two records with the same QNAM for the same IDVAR/IDVARVAL within a USUBJID and domain [Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/assumptions.md -- overview].
- Grouping variables (e.g., --GRPID) may be used in IDVAR to relate one supplemental value to multiple parent records; when domains are split and IDVAR is other than --SEQ, care is needed so parent values remain unique across the split datasets [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.5; chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.1.7 Splitting Domains].

results.answer:
## Linking mechanism in AP domains

**1. AP domains reuse subject-data structures with an `AP` prefix.**
AP datasets represent data about individuals other than study subjects who can be associated with a study, a particular study subject, or a device used in the study. Their structures are based on the structures used for study subjects — either the general observation classes (Interventions, Events, Findings) or special-purpose domain structures — with the domain code prefixed by `AP` (e.g., associated-persons demographics = `APDM`) [Source: model/04_associated_persons.md].

**2. The associated person is identified by APID, not USUBJID.**
APID (Associated Person Identifier, Char, Identifier) identifies a single associated person, a group of associated persons, or a pool of associated persons. APID is only allowed in AP domains (it was removed from the "Identifiers for All Classes" section for that reason). If APID identifies a pool, POOLDEF records must exist for each associated person [Source: model/04_associated_persons.md].

**3. Three linking variables carry the association: RSUBJID, RDEVID, SREL.**

| Variable | Label | Type | Role | Function |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RSUBJID | Related Subject or Pool Identifier | Char | Identifier | Identifies the related study subject or pool; populated with the USUBJID of the related subject or the POOLID of the related pool. Null when the associated person is related to the study but not to any study subject. |
| RDEVID | Related Device Identifier | Char | Identifier | Identifies a related device; populated with the SPDEVID of the related device. |
| SREL | Subject, Device, or Study Relationship | Char | Identifier (per the AP variable table) | Describes the relationship of the associated person(s) to whatever is populated: to the subject/pool in RSUBJID, or to the device in RDEVID, or — if RSUBJID and RDEVID are both null — to the study identified in STUDYID. |

[Source: model/04_associated_persons.md]

## Role of RSUBJID and SREL, precisely

- **RSUBJID = the pointer.** It supplies the *target* of the link (a USUBJID, or a POOLID for a pool of subjects) [Source: model/04_associated_persons.md]. In RELSUB the analogous variable is defined as "Identifier used to identify a related subject or pool of subjects. RSUBJID will be populated with either the USUBJID of the related subject or the POOLID of the related pool" — Type Char, Role Identifier, Core Req [Source: domains/RELSUB/spec.md].
- **SREL = the semantics of the pointer.** It qualifies *what kind of* relationship exists, and its meaning is conditional on which of RSUBJID/RDEVID is populated (subject/pool → device → study, in that fallback order) [Source: model/04_associated_persons.md].

## Where multiple/collected AP relationships live: APRELSUB

Relationships of an associated person to study subjects may be represented in the Associated Persons Relationships dataset; when an individual has multiple collected relationships to a study subject or subjects, those multiple relationships **must** be represented in that relationships dataset [Source: model/04_associated_persons.md].

**APRELSUB — Associated Persons Related Subjects**, structure: one record per associated person relationship [Source: model/06_relationship_datasets.md]:

| # | Variable | Label | Type | Role |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | STUDYID | Study Identifier | Char | Identifier |
| 2 | APID | Associated Person Identifier | Char | Identifier |
| 3 | RSUBJID | Related Subject or Pool Identifier | Char | Identifier |
| 4 | RDEVID | Related Device Identifier | Char | Identifier |
| 5 | SREL | Subject, Device, or Study Relationship | Char | Record Qualifier |

[Source: model/06_relationship_datasets.md]

Note the Role discrepancy across sources for SREL: the AP variables table lists SREL with Role Identifier [Source: model/04_associated_persons.md], while the APRELSUB dataset table and the RELSUB specification list it as Record Qualifier [Source: model/06_relationship_datasets.md] [Source: domains/RELSUB/spec.md].

## Boundary with RELSUB (subject-to-subject)

RELSUB is only for relationships between persons **both of whom are study subjects**. A relationship between a study subject and a person who is **not** a study subject may not be represented in RELSUB; this may only be reported in APRELSUB [Source: domains/RELSUB/assumptions.md] [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md]. So the non-subject ↔ subject link is exclusively an AP/APRELSUB construct.

Other RELSUB conventions that are useful context (stated for RELSUB, not asserted for APRELSUB): RSUBJID must be a USUBJID value present in DM and must be populated in every record; each subject-subject relationship is stored as 2 directional records with SREL expressed from each subject's viewpoint (e.g., "MOTHER, BIOLOGICAL" / "CHILD, BIOLOGICAL") [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md] [Source: domains/RELSUB/assumptions.md].

## Controlled terminology for SREL

In RELSUB, SREL carries controlled terminology **C100130** (Core: Req) [Source: domains/RELSUB/spec.md] [Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md], and values of SREL should be taken from the CDISC Controlled Terminology codelist RELSUB wherever possible; if no appropriate term exists, another term may be used, but the SREL term must not be *less specific* than the verbatim term collected (e.g., do not code "RELATIVE, FIRST DEGREE" when "brother" was collected) [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md]. The retrieved context does not state a codelist code for SREL as used in AP domains/APRELSUB — confirm in the terminology file.

## Caveat on scope

AP domains conform to the same general observation class models, variables, roles, and controlled terminology as subject data, but **AP domains are not part of the core SDTMIG for human clinical trials**; additional implementation guidance is in the SDTM Implementation Guide: Associated Persons (SDTMIG-AP) [Source: model/04_associated_persons.md].

## Rules for `--TESTCD` Values

### Length
- Values of `--TESTCD` **must be limited to 8 characters** [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.2.1 Variable-Naming Conventions].
- Because the limit is fixed, the variable **length can always be set to 8** for `--TESTCD` (and `IDVAR`), rather than using the SAS v5 transport maximum of 200 [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.2.9 Variable Lengths]. Note that "length" in the SDTMIG refers to length in **bytes of ASCII character strings** [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.2.9 Variable Lengths].

### Allowed characters
- The value **cannot start with a number** (e.g., "1TEST" is not valid) [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.2.1 Variable-Naming Conventions].
- The value **cannot contain characters other than letters, numbers, or underscores** [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.2.1 Variable-Naming Conventions].

### Rationale
- These restrictions exist to avoid possible incompatibility with **SAS v5 transport files**, and will remain in effect until other formats (e.g., Dataset-XML) become acceptable to regulatory authorities [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.2.1 Variable-Naming Conventions].
- The practical driver is that `--TESTCD` is designed to be usable as a **column name** when transposing a dataset from vertical (normalized) to horizontal format [Source: domains/VS/spec.md -- VSTESTCD].

### Related conventions
- **`QNAM`**: Because QNAM serves the same purpose as `--TESTCD` within Supplemental Qualifier datasets, values of QNAM are subject to the **same restrictions** as `--TESTCD` [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.2.1 Variable-Naming Conventions].
- **Other "CD" variables are NOT subject to the `--TESTCD` character restrictions**:
  - `ETCD` (companion to ELEMENT) and `TSPARMCD` (companion to TSPARM): limited to 8 characters, but **no** character restrictions [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.2.1 Variable-Naming Conventions].
  - `ARMCD` (and `ACTARMCD`): limited to **20 characters**, with no character restrictions — the longer limit accommodates crossover-trial arm codes (e.g., a 7-period crossover using 2-character treatment abbreviations with separating hyphens = 20 characters) [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.2.1 Variable-Naming Conventions].
- **Companion `--TEST`**: contains the full descriptive name of the test; `--TEST` cannot be longer than **40 characters** [Source: domains/CV/spec.md -- CVTEST]. Both `--TESTCD` and `--TEST` are subject to controlled terminology where available [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.2.1 Variable-Naming Conventions].
- Naming/format/terminology usage for the same type of data should be **consistent within and across studies** in a submission, including custom domains and Supplemental Qualifiers [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.2.1 Variable-Naming Conventions].

### Typical attributes of a `--TESTCD` variable
Illustrated by `VSTESTCD` — **Label:** Vital Signs Test Short Name; **Type:** Char; **Role:** Topic; **Core:** Req; **Controlled Terms:** C66741; examples "SYSBP", "DIABP", "BMI" [Source: domains/VS/spec.md -- VSTESTCD]. Some domains (e.g., `QSTESTCD`, `FTTESTCD`) have no single codelist in the spec because controlled terminology is published in **separate codelists per questionnaire/instrument** [Source: domains/QS/spec.md -- QSTESTCD] [Source: domains/FT/spec.md -- FTTESTCD].

## Representing Missing Values

SDTM represents missing values as **null** (an empty value) — there is no special missing-value code or placeholder. [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.2.5 Convention for Missing Values]

Use the completion-status and reason-not-done qualifiers of the relevant Findings domain:

### Variable characteristics (illustrated with MBSTAT)

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| Label | Completion Status |
| Type | Char |
| Controlled Terms | C66789 (Not Done) |
| Role | Record Qualifier |
| Core | Perm |

CDISC Notes: "Used to indicate that a question was not asked or a test was not done, or that a test was attempted but did not generate a result. Should be null or have a value of 'NOT DONE'." [Source: domains/MB/spec.md -- MBSTAT]

The **Not Done codelist (C66789)** is the controlled terminology governing --STAT (e.g., it is referenced for MISTAT in the Microscopic Findings domain). [Source: domains/MI/spec.md -- Controlled Terminology]

Note that --STAT is typically **Perm** core, so it is populated only when needed; when a test *was* done and produced a result, --STAT is left null. [Source: domains/MB/spec.md -- MBSTAT]

## Related Consideration: Null Columns and Core Designation

Whether a null-valued variable must still appear in the dataset depends on its Core designation:

- **Req** — must always be populated; cannot be null for any record.
- **Exp** — must be included in the dataset; may contain nulls. If the study does not include the data item at all, a null column must still be included and a comment added in the Define-XML document.
- **Perm** — include (even if null) if the study collected the data item; if the study did not collect it, do not include the variable and do not declare it in Define-XML.

[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.1.5 SDTM Core Designations]

results.answer:
## Convention for "Yes"/"No" Values in SDTM

### General rule: populate both responses

Variables whose response is "Yes" or "No" ("Y" or "N") **should normally be populated for both "Y" and "N" responses**. The rationale is to eliminate confusion regarding whether a blank response indicates "N" or is a missing value [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.3.7 Use of "Yes" and "No" Values].

### Exception: when only one value is unambiguous

Some variables are collected or derived in a manner that allows only 1 response — for example, when a single checkbox indicates "Yes". In such situations, **where it is unambiguous to populate only the response of interest, it is permissible to populate only 1 value ("Y" or "N") and leave the alternate value blank** [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.3.7 Use of "Yes" and "No" Values].

**Cited example:** Last Observation Before Exposure Flag (`--LOBXFL`), where a value of "N" is not necessary to indicate that a value is not the last observation before exposure — so populating only "Y" is acceptable [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.3.7 Use of "Yes" and "No" Values].

### Extending the permissible values

Permissible values for variables with controlled terms of "Y" or "N" **may be extended to include "U" or "NA"** if it is the sponsor's practice to explicitly collect or derive values indicating "Unknown" or "Not Applicable" for that variable [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.3.7 Use of "Yes" and "No" Values].

### Relevant controlled terminology

| Codelist | Code | Extensible | Submission Values |
|---|---|---|---|
| No Yes Response | C66742 | No | N, NA, U, Y |

Value-level codes visible in the source: N = C49487 ("No"), NA = C48660 ("Not Applicable"), U = C17998 ("Unknown"), Y = C49488 ("Yes") [Source: terminology/core/general_part4.md -- No Yes Response].

This codelist is referenced by a large number of variables across domains, including the AE seriousness/qualifier flags (AESER, AESDTH, AESHOSP, AESLIFE, AESDISAB, AESCONG, AESMIE, AECONTRT, AEPRESP, ...), the `--OCCUR` and `--PRESP` pairs in Interventions/Events domains (CMOCCUR/CMPRESP, MHOCCUR/MHPRESP, PROCCUR/PRPRESP, etc.), and Findings flags such as `--BLFL`, `--DRVFL`, `--LOBXFL`, `--CLSIG`, and `--FAST` [Source: terminology/core/general_part4.md -- No Yes Response].

**Note:** Some flag variables in the specs are restricted to a "Y"-only subset codelist rather than the full C66742 list; always confirm the exact Controlled Terms entry in the relevant `domains/{DOMAIN}/spec.md` for the specific variable.

results.answer:
## Rules Governing the Two-Character Domain Identifier

### Character composition rules

The 2-character domain code is constrained as follows:

- **First character:** limited to **A–Z** only.
- **Second character:** limited to **A–Z or 0–9**.
- **No other characters are allowed** (no lowercase letters, no underscores, no special characters).

The reason for this restriction is compatibility with **SAS v5 transport files** and with the file-naming requirements of the **Electronic Common Technical Document (eCTD)** [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.2.2 Two-character Domain Identifier].

### Use as a variable-name prefix

- The 2-character domain identifier is used as a prefix in most variable names, in order to minimize the risk of difficulty when merging/joining domains for reporting purposes [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.2.2 Two-character Domain Identifier].
- Domain specification tables (Sections 5–9 of the SDTMIG) already contain the complete variable names. However, when sponsors **add SDTM variables to standard domains or create custom domains** based on the general observation classes, they must **replace the "--" prefix** in the SDTM General Observation Class, Timing, and Identifier variable tables with the 2-character **DOMAIN** value for that domain/dataset [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.2.2 Two-character Domain Identifier].

### Exceptions to the prefixing convention

The following are *not* prefixed with the domain code [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.2.2 Two-character Domain Identifier]:

- Required Identifiers: **STUDYID, DOMAIN, USUBJID** — because they are typically used as merge/join keys.
- Commonly used grouping and merge keys (e.g., **VISIT, VISITNUM, VISITDY**).
- All **DM** domain variables other than **DMDTC** and **DMDY**.
- All variables in **RELREC** and **SUPPQUAL**, and some variables in the Comments and Trial Design datasets.

Conversely, **--SEQ** and the optional Identifiers **--GRPID** and **--REFID** *are* prefixed, because they may be used as keys when relating observations across domains [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.2.2 Two-character Domain Identifier].

### The DOMAIN variable itself

In each domain's specification, DOMAIN is defined as:

- **Label:** Domain Abbreviation
- **Type:** Char
- **Role:** Identifier
- **Core:** Req
- **Controlled Terms:** (none listed at variable level)
- **CDISC Notes:** "Two-character abbreviation for the domain." [Source: domains/LB/spec.md -- DOMAIN]
