results.answer_preview:
## RELREC — Purpose and Structure

**Description/Overview:** "A dataset used to describe relationships between records for a subject within or across domains, and relationships of records across datasets." **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.2.1 Related Records (RELREC)]**

**Specification:** `relrec.xpt`, Related Records — **Class: Relationship**. Structure: **one record per related record, group of records or dataset**, Tabulation. **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.2.1 Related Records (RELREC)]** **[Source: model/06_relationship_datasets.md -- 6.1 Related Records (REL
results.answer:
## RELREC — Purpose and Structure

**Description/Overview:** "A dataset used to describe relationships between records for a subject within or across domains, and relationships of records across datasets." **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.2.1 Related Records (RELREC)]**

**Specification:** `relrec.xpt`, Related Records — **Class: Relationship**. Structure: **one record per related record, group of records or dataset**, Tabulation. **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.2.1 Related Records (RELREC)]** **[Source: model/06_relationship_datasets.md -- 6.1 Related Records (RELREC)]** (Note: the narrative text in Section 8.2 and the RELREC assumptions refer to it colloquially as a "special-purpose dataset," but the dataset-level Class designation is Relationship.)

### Variables (SDTMIG v3.4)

| Variable | Label | Type | CT | Role | Core |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| STUDYID | Study Identifier | Char | | Identifier | Req |
| RDOMAIN | Related Domain Abbreviation | Char | (DOMAIN) | Identifier | Req |
| USUBJID | Unique Subject Identifier | Char | | Identifier | Exp |
| IDVAR | Identifying Variable | Char | * | Identifier | Req |
| IDVARVAL | Identifying Variable Value | Char | | Identifier | Exp |
| RELTYPE | Relationship Type | Char | (RELTYPE) | Record Qualifier | Exp |
| RELID | Relationship Identifier | Char | | Record Qualifier | Req |

**[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.2.1 Related Records (RELREC)]**

The SDTM v2.0 model version of the dataset carries 10 variables, adding APID, POOLID, and SPDEVID as alternative subject/device identifiers (USUBJID is null for dataset-level relationships), and states that RELID should be unique within the ID variable that is the subject of the relationship (e.g., USUBJID, APID, POOLID, SPDEVID). **[Source: model/06_relationship_datasets.md -- 6.1 Related Records (RELREC)]**

Controlled terminology referenced: **SDTM Domain Abbreviation (C66734)** for RDOMAIN and **Relationship Type (C78737)** for RELTYPE. **[Source: domains/RELREC/spec.md -- Controlled Terminology]** **[Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- RELREC — Related Records (Relationship)]**

---

## Use Case 1: Relating Peer Records (within/across domains)

A relationship is defined by adding **one record to RELREC for each record to be related**, and assigning a unique character identifier for the relationship in **RELID**. RELID is sponsor-chosen but **must be identical for all related records within USUBJID**; a consistent naming convention is recommended (e.g., all letters, all numbers, capitalized). **[Source: domains/RELREC/assumptions.md -- overview]** **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.1.1 --GRPID Example]**

Records expressing the relationship are keyed by **STUDYID, RDOMAIN, USUBJID, IDVAR, IDVARVAL**:
- **IDVAR** names the identifying variable in the general-observation-class dataset that identifies the related record(s) (e.g., --SEQ, --GRPID); **IDVARVAL** holds its value. **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.2.1 Related Records (RELREC)]**
- Single records → use a unique-record identifier such as **--SEQ** (required in all domains except DM).
- Groups of records → use a grouping variable such as **--GRPID**, which can be more efficient (e.g., relating an AE to a group of concomitant medications taken to treat it).
- **--REFID** (sponsor-defined or external identifier, e.g., lab specimen or ECG identifiers) may also be used in IDVAR; it is permissible in all general-observation-class domains but never required. **[Source: domains/RELREC/assumptions.md -- overview]**

RELREC should be used to represent (a) explicit collected relationships (e.g., CM taken as a result of an AE), or (b) information whose nature requires multiple datasets (see Relating Datasets). Relationships in RELREC are **collected** relationships — via explicit references/checkboxes on the CRF, or by CRF design (e.g., vital signs captured during an exercise stress test). **[Source: domains/RELREC/assumptions.md -- overview]**

**Example (peer records, USUBJID = 123456):** one AE participating in two separate relationships — with 2 CM records (RELID=1) and with 2 LB records (RELID=2):

| Row | STUDYID | RDOMAIN | USUBJID | IDVAR | IDVARVAL | RELTYPE | RELID |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | EFC1234 | AE | 123456 | AESEQ | 5 | | 1 |
| 2 | EFC1234 | CM | 123456 | CMSEQ | 11 | | 1 |
| 3 | EFC1234 | CM | 123456 | CMSEQ | 12 | | 1 |
| 4 | EFC1234 | AE | 123456 | AESEQ | 5 | | 2 |
| 5 | EFC1234 | LB | 123456 | LBSEQ | 47 | | 2 |
| 6 | EFC1234 | LB | 123456 | LBSEQ | 48 | | 2 |

Using CMGRPID="COMBO1" in IDVAR/IDVARVAL collapses the two CM rows into one, reducing 5 RELREC records to 4. Note RELTYPE is null for peer-record relationships. **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.2.2 RELREC Dataset Examples]**

---

## Use Case 2: Relating Datasets

RELREC can identify relationships **between datasets** (e.g., one-to-many/parent-child) by including **a single record per related dataset** that identifies the key(s) usable to relate the respective records. This should only be done when the sponsor has found it necessary to split related information across datasets that may need to be examined together for analysis or proper interpretation. **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.3 Relating Datasets Using RELREC]** **[Source: domains/RELREC/assumptions.md -- overview]**

**RELTYPE** identifies the hierarchical level of the records in the relationship; allowable values are **ONE** and **MANY** (controlled terminology expected), and it is used **only** for dataset-to-dataset relationships. The value pairs define how a merge/join would be written and its result: ONE–ONE, ONE–MANY, MANY–ONE, MANY–MANY. **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.2.1 Related Records (RELREC)]** **[Source: model/06_relationship_datasets.md -- 6.1 Related Records (RELREC)]** **[Source: domains/RELREC/assumptions.md -- overview]**

**When RELREC is NOT needed:** associations from **SUPP--** datasets or the **CO** dataset back to their parent general-observation-class or special-purpose domain records do not require RELREC, because those datasets already contain the parent record's key variable identifiers. **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.3 Relating Datasets Using RELREC]**

**Typical dataset-to-dataset applications:**
- **TU ↔ TR** via **TRLNKID**, and **TR ↔ RS** via **TRLNKGRP** — a dataset-to-dataset RELREC link is the most appropriate mechanism, since --GRPID, --REFID, and --SPID may be used for other purposes. **[Source: domains/TR/assumptions.md -- item_1]** **[Source: domains/TR/assumptions.md -- item_2]**
- **RS**: **RSLNKGRP** links findings records (e.g., TR, LB) that contribute to an RS record; records should exist in RELREC to support this. A RELREC relationship may also be defined using **RSLNKID**. **[Source: domains/RS/assumptions.md -- item_4]**
- **SS**: RELREC may be used to link status assessments with data in other domains collected as a result of the assessment. **[Source: domains/SS/assumptions.md -- item_2]**
- Further examples: Disposition (Section 6.2.4, Example 4) and the PK examples in Section 6.3.5.9.3, "Relating PP Records to PC Records." **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.2.2 RELREC Dataset Examples]**

Note that **RELSPEC** (Related Specimens) only maintains relationships between specimens and therefore does not require the additional variables used in RELREC. **[Source: domains/RELSPEC/assumptions.md -- item_2]**

---

## What RDOMAIN Does

- **Label:** Related Domain Abbreviation; **Type:** Char; **Controlled Terms:** (DOMAIN) — SDTM Domain Abbreviation, codelist **C66734**; **Role:** Identifier (in the RELREC specification table); **Core:** Req. **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.2.1 Related Records (RELREC)]** **[Source: domains/RELREC/spec.md -- Controlled Terminology]**
- **CDISC Notes:** "Abbreviation for the domain of the parent record(s)." **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.2.1 Related Records (RELREC)]** The SDTM v2.0 model describes it as the 2-character abbreviation for the domain of the parent record(s). **[Source: model/06_relationship_datasets.md -- 6.1 Related Records (RELREC)]**
- **Function:** Together with STUDYID, USUBJID, IDVAR, and IDVARVAL, RDOMAIN identifies *which domain/dataset* the record being related lives in — it tells the consumer which dataset to look in and which domain-prefixed identifying variable (e.g., AESEQ, CMSEQ, LBSEQ, CMGRPID) IDVAR refers to. **[Source: domains/RELREC/assumptions.md -- overview]** **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.2.

results.answer:
## Core definitions

**Intervention** — "An intervention is something that is done to a subject (possibly by the subject) that is expected to have a physiological effect. This concept of intended effect makes interventions relatively easy to recognize, although there are gray areas around some testing procedures." [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.6.1 Guidelines for Determining the General Observation Class]

The SDTM model states the Interventions observation class "represents investigational, therapeutic, and other treatments that are administered to or used by a subject (with some actual or expected physiological effect). This includes treatments specified by the study protocol (i.e., 'exposure')." Its structure is **One Record per Constant-dosing Interval or Intervention Episode**, and its Topic variable is **--TRT** (Name of Treatment). [Source: model/02_observation_classes.md -- 3.1.1 The Interventions Observation Class]

At the class-summary level: Interventions capture "Investigational, therapeutic, and other treatments administered to or used by a subject (with some actual or expected physiological effect), including treatments that are self-administered by the subject (i.e., use of alcohol, tobacco, or caffeine)" — e.g., EX, CM, PR. [Source: chapters/ch02_fundamentals.md -- 2.3 The General Observation Classes]

**Event** — "An event is something that happens to a subject spontaneously. Most, although not all, events data captured in clinical trials is about medical events. Because many medical events must, by regulation, be treated as adverse events, a new Events domain will be created only for events that are clearly not adverse events; the existing Medical History (MH) and Clinical Events (CE) domains are the appropriate places to store most medical events that are not adverse events." [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.6.1 Guidelines for Determining the General Observation Class]

At the class-summary level, Events capture "Planned protocol milestones and occurrences, conditions, or incidents independent of planned evaluations" — e.g., AE, DS, MH. [Source: chapters/ch02_fundamentals.md -- 2.3 The General Observation Classes]

**Findings (for contrast)** — "Findings general observation class data include measurements, tests, assessments, or examinations performed on a subject in the clinical trial. These may be performed on the subject as a whole (e.g., height, heart rate), or on a specimen taken from a subject (e.g., blood sample, ECG tracing, tissue sample). Sometimes the relationship between a subject and a finding is less direct; a finding may be about an event that happened to the subject or an intervention received." [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.6.1 Guidelines for Determining the General Observation Class]

## Key discriminator: intended physiological effect vs. spontaneity

- Interventions = **done to/by** the subject, with **actual or expected physiological effect** (intentional act). [Source: model/02_observation_classes.md -- 3.1.1 The Interventions Observation Class]
- Events = **happen to** the subject **spontaneously** / independently of planned evaluations. [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.6.1 Guidelines for Determining the General Observation Class] [Source: chapters/ch02_fundamentals.md -- 2.3 The General Observation Classes]

## Method of determination — content, not structure

Begin by considering "the content of the information in the light of the definitions of the 3 general observation classes ... rather than by trying to deduce the class from the information's physical structure; physical structure can sometimes be misleading. For example, from a structural standpoint, one might expect events observations to include a start and stop date. However, medical history data (data about previous conditions or events) is events data regardless of whether dates were collected." [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.6.1 Guidelines for Determining the General Observation Class]

Gray areas: testing procedures designed to produce a physiological effect (e.g., exercise stress tests) yield **findings** for the measurements, "although some aspects of the procedure might be modeled as interventions." [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.6.1 Guidelines for Determining the General Observation Class]

## Supporting structural clues (not definitive)

Section 8.6.3 offers questions to help place data; the structure "although not definitive, will often help determine whether the data represent an event or a finding":
- Measurement with units → Finding (a "No" answer is inconclusive).
- Log forms (completed over the course of the study rather than at a single visit) → Events or Interventions data; dates are usually start/end dates of the event or intervention. Observations made at individual visits are usually planned findings.
- Verbatim text collected then coded → suggests Events or Interventions data; note that for Events and Interventions the **topic variable** is coded, whereas for Findings the **result** is coded.
[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.6.3 Guidelines for Differentiating Between Interventions, Events, Findings, and Findings About Events or Interventions]

Note that assessments of *part* of an event/intervention (different timing from the event as a whole) go to FA, while assessments of the whole are built into the Events/Interventions models as qualifiers (e.g., OCCUR, SEV, TOXGR). [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.6.3 Guidelines for Differentiating Between Interventions, Events, Findings, and Findings About Events or Interventions] [Source: domains/FA/assumptions.md -- item_4]

Additional pointers: Section 2.6 (Creating a New Domain) governs when to create a new domain [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.6.1 Guidelines for Determining the General Observation Class]; general assumptions for domains based on the general observation classes are in Section 4 [Source: chapters/ch02_fundamentals.md -- 2.3 The General Observation Classes]; and for prespecified vs. free-text interventions/events, --PRESP, --OCCUR, --STAT, and --REASND apply to both classes [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.5.7 Presence or Absence of Prespecified Interventions and Events].

results.answer:
## Associated Persons (AP) in SDTM

**Definition:** Associated persons are individuals *other than study subjects* who can be associated with a study, a particular study subject, or a device used in the study [Source: model/04_associated_persons.md -- Overview].

The structures of SDTM datasets representing associated-persons data are based on the structures used for study-subject data — either the general observation class structures (Interventions, Events, Findings) or the special-purpose domain structures. AP domains are created using SDTM variables, with the application of specific AP rules [Source: model/04_associated_persons.md -- Overview].

### Naming convention relative to standard domain codes

AP domains use the domain code prefix **`AP`** followed by the relevant standard domain code. For example, associated persons demographics would use **`APDM`** [Source: model/04_associated_persons.md -- Overview].

### AP-specific identifier variables

| Variable | Label | Type | Role | Notes |
|----------|-------|------|------|-------|
| APID | Associated Persons Identifier | Char | Identifier | Identifier for a single associated person, a group of associated persons, or a pool of associated persons. If APID identifies a pool, POOLDEF records must exist for each associated person. Used instead of USUBJID; APID is only allowed in AP domains (it was removed from Section 3.1.4, Identifiers for All Classes, but is still listed in Section 3 as an identifier). |
| RSUBJID | Related Subject or Pool Identifier | Char | Identifier | Identifier for a related subject or pool of subjects; may be populated with the USUBJID of the related subject or the POOLID of the related pool. Null for associated persons related to the study but not to any study subject. |
| RDEVID | Related Device Identifier | Char | Identifier | Identifier for a related device; populated with the SPDEVID of the related device. |
| SREL | Subject, Device, or Study Relationship | Char | Identifier | If RSUBJID is populated, describes the relationship of the associated person(s) to that subject/pool; if RDEVID is populated, describes the relationship to that device; if both are null, describes the relationship to the study identified in STUDYID. |

[Source: model/04_associated_persons.md -- Overview]

### Key principles and scope

- AP domains conform to the same general observation class models used for subject data, with the same variables, roles, and controlled terminology [Source: model/04_associated_persons.md -- Overview].
- Relationships of an associated person to study subjects may be represented in the Associated Persons Relationships dataset; when an individual has multiple collected relationships to a study subject or subjects, those multiple relationships must be represented in that relationships dataset [Source: model/04_associated_persons.md -- Overview].
- **AP domains are not part of the core SDTMIG for human clinical trials**; additional implementation guidance is provided in the SDTM Implementation Guide: Associated Persons (**SDTMIG-AP**) [Source: model/04_associated_persons.md -- Overview], which is described as covering "data about persons who are not study subjects" [Source: chapters/ch01_introduction.md -- 1.3 Relationship to Prior CDISC Documents].

### Related naming context

Standard domain codes come from the SDTM Domain Abbreviation codelist (C66734) [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.1.6 Additional Guidance on Dataset Naming]. Note that the 2-character domain code convention (limited to A-Z first character, A-Z/0-9 second character) applies to standard/custom GOC domains [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.2.2 Two-character Domain Identifier]; AP dataset names extend this with the `AP` prefix as described above. The retrieved context does not give further detail on variable prefixing within AP datasets — consult the SDTMIG-AP for that.

results.answer:
## Expected (Exp) Core Designation

**Definition:** An **Expected** variable is any variable necessary to make a record useful in the context of a specific domain. Expected variables may contain some null values, but in most cases will not contain null values for every record. [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.1.5 SDTM Core Designations]

Expected is one of the three categories specified in the **Core** column of the domain models, alongside **Req** (Required) and **Perm** (Permissible). [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.1.5 SDTM Core Designations]

### Rules for Exp variables

| Aspect | Rule |
|--------|------|
| Inclusion | Must be included in the dataset |
| Population | Value should be populated when available; null values are allowed when data are not collected/not applicable |
| Study does not collect the data item | A **null column must still be included** in the dataset, **and a comment must be included in the Define-XML document** stating that the study does not include the data item |

[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.1.5 SDTM Core Designations]

### Contrast with the other Core values

- **Req (Required):** basic to the identification of a data record (essential key variables and the topic variable) or necessary to make the record meaningful; must always be included and **cannot be null for any record**. [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.1.5 SDTM Core Designations]
- **Perm (Permissible):** if the study includes the data item, the variable must be included (even if null) and declared in Define-XML; if the study did **not** collect it, the variable should **not** be included in the dataset and should **not** be declared in Define-XML. [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.1.5 SDTM Core Designations] [Source: chapters/ch02_fundamentals.md -- 2.5 The SDTM Standard Domain Models]

This is the key operational difference: for **Exp**, an uncollected item still yields a null column plus a Define-XML comment; for **Perm**, an uncollected item yields no column at all.

### Related notes

- The Core column is one of the two shaded columns in the CDISC domain models that are not sent to the FDA but assist sponsors (the other being CDISC Notes); it indicates how a variable is classified per Section 4.1.5. [Source: chapters/ch03_submitting_data.md -- 3.1 Standard Metadata for Dataset Contents and Attributes]
- A null value is implied for any list of controlled terms unless the variable is "Required" — i.e., for Exp and Perm variables with a codelist, null is permitted and should not be listed in the permissible value set in Define-XML. [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.3.3 Controlled Terminology Values]

results.answer:
## Decision Framework: SUPP-- vs. FA

SDTM does not allow adding new variables to a domain, so any assessment of an event that is not already a standard Events-class qualifier must go somewhere else — either as a non-standard variable (NSV) in the SUPP-- dataset, or as a record in a Findings About domain. The choice is driven primarily by **timing**, **structural complexity (number of variables needed)**, and **whether the data are a qualifier of the parent record or a separate observation**.

### Step 0 — First check: is there already a standard qualifier?
Some assessments of an event have been built into the SDTM Events model as qualifiers (e.g., severity, relationship to study treatment) rather than being treated as findings about events. [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md — 8.6.3] If the assessment applies to the **event as a whole** and a standard variable exists, use it in the parent Events domain. In 8.6.3 the diagnostic question is posed directly: "If this is data about an event, does it apply to the event as a whole? A 'Yes' answer suggests this is traditional Events general observation class [data]." [Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md — 8.6.3]

### Criteria that push the data into FA

**Criterion 1 — Different timing from the event as a whole.**
"The Findings About Events or Interventions structure ... is intended ... to be used when findings about an event or intervention need to be captured." A finding that is about *part* of an event, rather than the event as a whole, meets this criterion — e.g., the severity of an individual symptom at a specific point in time, repeated assessments of intermittent symptoms, or repeated fixed-timepoint assessments after a short-duration event (infusion reaction, seizure). A finding that **summarizes multiple occurrences** (e.g., maximum headache severity in a post-dose window) also meets this criterion. [Source: domains/FA/assumptions.md — item_6 / §6.4.1]

**Criterion 2 — More than one variable is needed for the representation.**
"An observation about an event or intervention which requires more than 1 variable for its representation, preventing its inclusion as a supplemental qualifier." The need to represent data requiring more than one variable in a findings-about structure, rather than by adding 2 or more supplemental qualifiers to the parent record, is the basis for this criterion. [Source: domains/FA/assumptions.md — item_6 / §6.4.1]

**Criterion 3 — Data or information that indicate the occurrence of pre-specified AEs.** [Source: domains/FA/assumptions.md — item_6 / §6.4.1] (Relevant because AE prohibits --OCCUR, --STAT, and --REASND, since AE contains only events that actually occurred. [Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md — item_10])

**RELMIDS consideration.** From the "Points to Consider": if the event or intervention is a disease milestone, RELMIDS is not included in that event/intervention record; if the relationship of a data item to the disease milestone (RELMIDS) is needed, "it can be represented in FA, but not as a supplemental qualifier to the parent record." [Source: chapters/ch02_fundamentals.md — Naming Findings About Domains / Points to Consider]

The same section frames the primary test as: "Does the data item have its own timing, separate from the timing of the event or intervention? If the data item represents some action during or after the event or intervention, it may be considered to have its own timing, and meet Criterion 1." It also acknowledges that "the choice between representing a data item as a supplemental qualifier or as a finding about an event or intervention may not be clear-cut." [Source: chapters/ch02_fundamentals.md]

### What belongs in SUPP-- instead

- **Additional qualifiers of the parent record.** "As the name suggests, this dataset is intended to capture additional qualifiers for an observation. **Data that represent separate observations should be treated as separate observations**" — i.e., not forced into SUPP--. [Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/assumptions.md — overview]
- **Attributions.** "An attribution is typically an interpretation or subjective classification of 1 or more observations by a specific evaluator, such as a flag that indicates whether an observation was considered to be clinically significant. ... SUPP-- provides a mechanism for incorporating as many attributions as are necessary," with QEVAL carrying the evaluator role (null for objective data). [Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/assumptions.md — overview]
- **Secondary evaluations of a standard qualifier.** Events/Interventions classes have no --EVAL variable, so all data are assumed attributed to the principal investigator; primary evaluation goes in the standard domain, secondary evaluation goes to SUPP-- with QNAM formed by appending "1" (replacing the last character if the name is already 8 characters, e.g., AESEV1, AEREL1, AERELNS1). [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md — 4.5.4]
- **Reasons not covered by standard variables** (e.g., QNAM "--REAS" for a reason for an Events-domain activity). [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md — 4.5.6]
- Note the uniqueness constraint: only one record per QNAM per parent record, so repeated/time-varying assessments cannot be stacked in SUPP-- — another practical reason such data must go to FA. [Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/assumptions.md — overview]

### Supporting structural questions (8.6.3)

| Question | Interpretation |
|---|---|
| Is this a measurement, with units, etc.? | "Yes" indicates a finding; if it measures some aspect of an event, it may be represented as a finding about the event. "No" is inconclusive. |
| Log form vs. per-visit CRF? | Log forms suggest Events/Interventions class; observations made at individual visits are usually planned findings. |
| What date/times are collected? | Start/end dates → event or intervention; dates of assessments → finding. |
| Is verbatim text collected and coded? | For Events/Interventions the **topic** variable is coded; for Findings the **result** is coded. |

[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md — 8.6.3]

### Consequences once FA is chosen

- FAOBJ (Object of the Observation, Char, Record Qualifier, **Req**) must be populated with the name of the event or intervention about which the finding was made; FATESTCD and --OBJ together define the topic, so **both are required on every record**. [Source: domains/FA/assumptions.md — item_6; model/02_observation_classes.md — §6.4.3; VARIABLE_INDEX.md — FA]
- "The --OBJ variable cannot be added to a standard Findings domain. A domain is either a Findings domain or a Findings About domain." [Source: chapters/ch02_fundamentals.md]
- When FA represents a finding about *part* of an event/intervention, FATEST/FATESTCD should reuse the variable name and label from the corresponding Events/Interventions domain (e.g., OCCUR = "Occurrence Indicator", SEV = "Severity/Intensity", TOXGR = "Toxicity Grade"). [Source: domains/FA/assumptions.md — item_4; model/02_observation_classes.md — §6.4.3]
- Certain qualifiers should generally not be used in FA: --BODSYS, --MODIFY, --SEV, --TOXGR. [Source: domains/FA/assumptions.md — item_6]
- FA records may or may not have a parent event record; linkage to a parent is via RELREC (record- or dataset-level). [Source: domains/FA/assumptions.md — item_6; chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md — 4.1.7]
- Naming/splitting: keep DOMAIN = "FA" and prefixes "FA", with dataset names like FACE, FAMH, FACM; or define a separate sponsor domain code not beginning with FA (e.g., SR). Split SUPP-- datasets follow (suppface.xpt, suppfamh.xpt, SUPPFACM), with RDOMAIN = "FA". [Source: chapters/ch02_fundamentals.md; chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md — 4.1.7]

### Summary rule of thumb

| Situation | Placement |
|---|---|
| Applies to event as a whole, standard qualifier exists | Parent Events domain variable |
| Applies to event as a whole, single extra qualifier, same timing, no standard variable | SUPP-- (QNAM/QVAL) |
| Subjective attribution / secondary evaluator's assessment | SUPP-- (QEVAL, QNAM+"1") |
| Own timing (snapshot/slice of the event, repeated or summarized assessments) | FA |
| Needs ≥2 variables to represent | FA |
| Indicates occurrence of pre-specified AEs | FA |
| RELMIDS linkage to a disease milestone needed | FA |

results.answer:
## Character Restrictions and Length Limits: "CD" Variables

SDTM variables ending in "CD" are "short" versions of their companion variables, but **only --TESTCD (and QNAM) carry the strict character-content restrictions**. [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.2.1 Variable-Naming Conventions]

### --TESTCD (and QNAM)

- Maximum **8 characters**
- **Cannot start with a number** (e.g., "1TEST" is invalid)
- **Cannot contain characters other than letters, numbers, or underscores**
- Rationale: avoid incompatibility with SAS v5 transport files, since --TESTCD values may be used as variable/column names when transposing a dataset from vertical to horizontal format. This limitation remains in effect until other formats (e.g., Dataset-XML) become acceptable to regulatory authorities.
- Because QNAM serves the same purpose as --TESTCD in supplemental qualifier datasets, QNAM values are subject to the same restrictions.

[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.2.1 Variable-Naming Conventions]

Examples of this rule stated at domain level: SCTESTCD, DDTESTCD, SRTESTCD, RSTESTCD, MSTESTCD all repeat "cannot be longer than 8 characters, nor can it start with a number... cannot contain characters other than letters, numbers, or underscores." [Source: domains/SC/spec.md -- SCTESTCD] [Source: domains/DD/spec.md -- DDTESTCD] [Source: domains/RS/spec.md -- RSTESTCD] [Source: domains/MS/spec.md -- MSTESTCD]

### ETCD and TSPARMCD

- Limited to **8 characters** (same length cap as --TESTCD)
- **No special character restrictions** — they are *not* subject to the --TESTCD content rules (no first-character or letters/numbers/underscore-only constraint)
- Values should be short for ease of use in programming, but it is **not expected that they will need to serve as variable names**

[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.2.1 Variable-Naming Conventions] [Source: domains/TE/spec.md -- ETCD] [Source: domains/TS/spec.md -- TSPARMCD]

- ETCD is the companion to ELEMENT; Role Topic, Type Char, Core Req in TE. [Source: domains/TE/spec.md -- ETCD]
- TSPARMCD is the companion to TSPARM; Role Topic, Type Char, Core Req, Controlled Terms C66738. Examples: "AGEMIN", "AGEMAX". [Source: domains/TS/spec.md -- TSPARMCD] A list of values for TSPARM/TSPARMCD is in CDISC Controlled Terminology. [Source: domains/TS/assumptions.md -- item_5]

### ARMCD (and ACTARMCD)

- Limited to **20 characters** — longer than other "short" variables
- **No special character restrictions**; not subject to the --TESTCD character rules
- Rationale: accommodate values needed for crossover trials — e.g., a 7-period crossover using 2-character treatment abbreviations separated by hyphens yields a 20-character value
- The **same rule applies to ACTARMCD**

[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.2.1 Variable-Naming Conventions] [Source: domains/TA/spec.md -- ARMCD] [Source: domains/DM/spec.md -- ARMCD] [Source: domains/DM/spec.md -- ACTARMCD]

ARMCD appears in DM, TA, and TV. [Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- §一 通用变量: ARMCD] It is Topic/Req in TA [Source: domains/TA/spec.md -- ARMCD] and Record Qualifier/Exp in DM and TV [Source: domains/DM/spec.md -- ARMCD] [Source: domains/TV/spec.md -- ARMCD].

### Summary Table

| Variable | Max length | Special character restrictions | May serve as a variable/column name? |
|---|---|---|---|
| --TESTCD / QNAM | 8 | Yes — no leading digit; letters, numbers, underscores only | Yes (vertical→horizontal transpose) |
| ETCD | 8 | No | Not expected |
| TSPARMCD | 8 | No | Not expected |
| ARMCD / ACTARMCD | 20 | No | Not expected |

[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.2.1 Variable-Naming Conventions]

**Note:** DM's ARMCD/ACTARMCD notes add a content constraint of a different kind (referential, not character-based): except in studies using multistage arm assignments, the value must be a value of ARMCD in the Trial Arms (TA) dataset; if the subject was not assigned to an arm (or, for ACTARMCD, followed a course not described by any planned arm), the variable is null and ARMNRS is populated. [Source: domains/DM/spec.md -- ARMCD] [Source: domains/DM/spec.md -- ACTARMCD] In TV, ARMCD should be null if visit timing does not depend on arm. [Source: domains/TV/spec.md -- ARMCD]

results.answer:
## Relative Timing Variables in SDTM

In the SDTM model, timing variables available to all 3 general observation classes are listed in SDTM Section 3.1.5. Within that list, the following are grouped under the heading **"Relative Timing Variables"** [Source: model/02_observation_classes.md -- 3.1.5 Timing Variables for All Classes]:

| # | Variable | Label | Type |
|---|----------|-------|------|
| 33 | --STRF | Start Relative to Reference Period | Char |
| 34 | --ENRF | End Relative to Reference Period | Char |
| 35 | --EVLINT | Evaluation Interval | Char |
| 36 | --EVINTX | Evaluation Interval Text | Char |
| 37 | --STRTPT | Start Relative to Reference Time Point | Char |

[Source: model/02_observation_classes.md -- 3.1.5 Timing Variables for All Classes]

The retrieved model excerpt is truncated after #37, but Section 4.4.7 confirms the group also includes the companion variables **--STTPT** (Start Reference Time Point), **--ENRTPT** (End Relative to Reference Time Point), and **--ENTPT** (End Reference Time Point) [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.4.7 Use of Relative Timing Variables].

---

### 1. Relative to the study reference *period*: --STRF / --ENRF

These represent timing of an observation relative to the **sponsor-defined study reference period** — the continuous period bounded by RFSTDTC and RFENDTC in DM — used when information such as "BEFORE", "PRIOR", "ONGOING", or "CONTINUING" is collected in lieu of a date [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.4.7 Use of Relative Timing Variables].

| Variable | Allowable Values | Purpose |
|----------|-----------------|---------|
| --STRF | BEFORE, DURING, DURING/AFTER, AFTER, UNKNOWN | Start relative to the sponsor-defined reference period |
| --ENRF | BEFORE, DURING, DURING/AFTER, AFTER, UNKNOWN | End relative to the sponsor-defined reference period |

[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.4.7 Use of Relative Timing Variables]

**Restriction:** although "COINCIDENT" and "ONGOING" exist in the STENRF codelist, they describe timing relative to a *point* in time rather than an *interval*, so they are **not appropriate for --ENRF** [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.4.7 Use of Relative Timing Variables].

**Attributes as implemented in domains** (e.g., CMSTRF, AGSTRF, CESTRF, SUSTRF): Type Char, **Controlled Terms: C66728**, Role **Timing**, Core **Perm**, with the note "Not all values of the codelist are allowable for this variable" [Source: domains/CM/spec.md -- CMSTRF] [Source: domains/AG/spec.md -- AGSTRF] [Source: domains/CE/spec.md -- CESTRF] [Source: domains/SU/spec.md -- SUSTRF].

### 2. Relative to a specific reference *time point*: --STRTPT/--STTPT and --ENRTPT/--ENTPT

--STRF/--ENRF only work when the assessment is coincident with the start/end of the study reference period; --STRTPT and --ENRTPT carry similar values but can be anchored to **any** timing description or date/time placed in --STTPT / --ENTPT [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.4.7 Use of Relative Timing Variables].

| Variable | Allowable Values | Purpose |
|----------|-----------------|---------|
| --STRTPT | BEFORE, COINCIDENT, AFTER, UNKNOWN | Start relative to a specific reference time point |
| --STTPT | (free text) | Description of the reference time point for --STRTPT |
| --ENRTPT | BEFORE, COINCIDENT, AFTER, ONGOING, UNKNOWN | End relative to a specific reference time point |
| --ENTPT | (free text) | Description of the reference time point for --ENRTPT |

[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.4.7 Use of Relative Timing Variables]

**Restrictions:**
- "DURING" and "DURING/AFTER" are in the STENRF codelist but describe an interval, so they are **not allowable for --STRTPT / --ENRTPT** [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.4.7 Use of Relative Timing Variables].
- If the reference time point corresponds to the date of collection/assessment, **AFTER is not valid for --STRTPT** (it would represent an event after the collection date); AFTER is valid only if the reference time point precedes the collection date [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.4.7 Use of Relative Timing Variables].
- Like --STRF, --STRTPT is implemented with Controlled Terms **C66728**, Role Timing, Core Perm, and the caveat that not all codelist values are allowable (e.g., RSSTRTPT) [Source: domains/RS/spec.md -- RSSTRTPT].

### 3. Evaluation interval: --EVLINT / --EVINTX

| Variable | Type | Notes |
|----------|------|-------|
| --EVLINT | Char | ISO 8601 duration or interval |
| --EVINTX | Char | Text description used when the interval cannot be represented in ISO 8601 |

[Source: model/02_observation_classes.md -- 3.1.5 Timing Variables for All Classes]

---

### Typical usage patterns

- **Medical History:** MHENRF when "Ongoing"/"Active" is coincident with the start of the study reference period (RFSTDTC); MHENRTPT with MHENTPT when "Ongoing" is relative to another date such as the screening visit. MHSTRF may be added when appropriate [Source: domains/MH/assumptions.md -- item_5]. Example: MHSTDTC = "2002", MHENRTPT = "ONGOING", with MHDTC = date of assessment [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.4.7 Use of Relative Timing Variables].
- **Adverse Events:** AEENRF when "Ongoing" is coincident with the end of the study reference period (RFENDTC); AEENRTPT with AEENTPT when "Ongoing" is relative to another date, e.g., AEENRTPT = "ONGOING", AEENTPT = "DATE OF LAST DOSE" [Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md -- item_5] [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.4.7 Use of Relative Timing Variables].
- **Concomitant Medications:** CMSTRF = "BEFORE", CMENRF = "DURING" for period-relative data; or CMENRTPT = "ONGOING" with CMENTPT = "2007-04-30" (the assessment date) when the end date is unknown [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.4.7 Use of Relative Timing Variables] [Source: domains/CM/assumptions.md -- item_4].
- **Clinical Events:** CESTRF/CEENRF for period-relative "Prior"/"Ongoing"; CESTRTPT+CESTTPT and/or CEENRTPT+CEENTPT when relative to other dates [Source: domains/CE/assumptions.md -- item_5].

### Two cautions

- Deriving --STRF/--ENRF even when dates are collected may blur the distinction between collected and derived values; such derivations are better placed in analysis datasets [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.4.7 Use of Relative Timing Variables].
- DM's RFSTDTC, RFENDTC, RFXSTDTC, etc. are date/time values but have a **Record Qualifier** role in DM and are **not** timing variables, since they are not intended for use in the general observation classes [Source: domains/DM/assumptions.md -- item_7].

*Note on terminology:* C66728 is the codelist code cited in the domain specs for these variables; the individual value names above are quoted from Section 4.4.7 — their per-term NCI codes must be confirmed in the SDTM Terminology file.

results.answer:
## LBORRES vs. LBSTRESC

**LBORRES — Result or Finding in Original Units**
- Order: 15; Type: Char; Role: Result Qualifier; Core: Exp; Controlled Terms: none
- CDISC Notes: "Result of the measurement or finding as originally received or collected." [Source: domains/LB/spec.md -- LBORRES]

**LBSTRESC — Character Result/Finding in Std Format**
- Order: 23; Type: Char; Role: Result Qualifier; Core: Exp; Controlled Terms: C102580
- CDISC Notes: Contains the result value for all findings, **copied or derived from LBORRES** in a standard format or standard units. LBSTRESC should store all results or findings in character format; if results are numeric they should **also** be stored in numeric format in LBSTRESN. Example given: results "NONE", "NEG", and "NEGATIVE" in LBORRES that effectively have the same meaning could all be represented in LBSTRESC as "NEGATIVE". [Source: domains/LB/spec.md -- LBSTRESC]

So the distinction is: LBORRES is the verbatim/as-received result in the units in which it was collected (uncontrolled), while LBSTRESC is the harmonized/standardized character representation (standard format and standard units, controlled terminology), with the numeric counterpart in LBSTRESN.

**LBSTRESN — Numeric Result/Finding in Standard Units**
- Order: 24; Type: Num; Role: Result Qualifier; Core: Exp
- "Used for continuous or numeric results or findings in standard format; copied in numeric format from LBSTRESC." [Source: domains/LB/spec.md -- LBSTRESN]

Illustration: a pregnancy test whose original result was "-" (negative sign) in LBORRES is standardized to the text value "NEGATIVE" in LBSTRESC. [Source: domains/LB/examples.md -- Example 3]

## Codelist referenced by LBSTRESC

LBSTRESC references **Laboratory Test Standard Character Result (C102580)**, which is **Extensible: Yes**, and is referenced by only that one variable (LB.LBSTRESC). [Source: domains/LB/spec.md -- Controlled Terminology] [Source: terminology/core/lb_part4.md -- Laboratory Test Standard Character Result] [Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- §三 CT 交叉引用: C102580]

## Standard result values in C102580

| Code | CDISC Submission Value | Definition (abbrev.) |
|------|------------------------|----------------------|
| C14157 | BORDERLINE | Straddling the dividing line between two categories. |
| C48658 | INDETERMINATE | Cannot distinguish between two or more possible values in the current context. |
| C50913 | INVALID | Not valid data. |
| C38757 | NEGATIVE | A finding of normality following an examination/investigation looking for the presence of a microorganism, disease, or condition. |
| C38758 | POSITIVE | An observation confirming something, such as the presence of a disease, condition, or microorganism. |
| C80218 | TRACE | A barely detectable amount. |

[Source: terminology/core/lb_part4.md -- Laboratory Test Standard Character Result]

For positive/negative findings specifically, the codelist supplies **POSITIVE**, **NEGATIVE**, plus the intermediate/qualifying values **BORDERLINE**, **TRACE**, **INDETERMINATE**, and **INVALID**. Because the codelist is extensible, sponsor-defined standardized character results may be added when no existing term applies.

## Related notes
- For non-continuous/descriptive tests (e.g., dipstick urine protein, urine color), the character reference range LBSTNRC may hold an ordinal range such as "NEGATIVE to TRACE" or a delimited set of normal values, while LBORNRLO/LBORNRHI/LBSTNRLO/LBSTNRHI are left null. [Source: domains/LB/assumptions.md -- item_2] [Source: domains/LB/spec.md -- LBSTNRC]
- LBSTNRLO/LBSTNRHI are the reference limits for LBSTRESC/LBSTRESN in standardized units and should be populated only for continuous results. [Source: domains/LB/spec.md -- LBSTNRLO]
- Where the result falls relative to the reference range is conveyed in LBNRIND (e.g., "HIGH", "LOW"), not in LBSTRESC. [Source: domains/LB/assumptions.md -- item_3]
- The same original-vs-standardized pattern applies in other Findings domains, e.g., MBSTRESC is copied/derived from MBORRES ("+3 MODERATE", "MOD", "MODERATE" → "MODERATE"). [Source: domains/MB/spec.md -- MBSTRESC]

## Purpose / Usage

- QSCAT identifies **which QRS instrument (questionnaire)** the item/question belongs to. It is a **Required** Grouping Qualifier in QS. [Source: domains/QS/spec.md -- QSCAT]
- The name of a QRS instrument is described under the variable --CAT in the relevant QRS domain (i.e., FT, QS, RS), and may be either abbreviations or longer names; sponsors should always reference CDISC Controlled Terminology. For QS specifically, the applicable codelist is **Category of Questionnaire** (the other QRS --CAT codelists being Category of Functional Test for FT and Category of Clinical Classification for RS). [Source: domains/QS/assumptions.md -- item_1]
- Finer granularity within an instrument is carried in **QSSCAT** (Subcategory for Question, Char, Grouping Qualifier, Perm), e.g., "MENTAL HEALTH", "DEPRESSION", "WORD RECALL". Note that --SCAT values are **not** in CDISC Controlled Terminology; they are controlled by the QRS supplements in which they are used. [Source: domains/QS/spec.md -- QSSCAT] [Source: domains/QS/assumptions.md -- item_2]
- QSCAT is also the usual basis for **splitting** the QS domain into physically separate datasets (e.g., QS36 for SF-36); when a domain is split on --CAT, --CAT must not be null. [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.1.7 Splitting Domains]
- QSCAT is frequently used as **IDVAR** in SUPPQS to attach instrument-level qualifiers (e.g., QNAM = QSLANG, questionnaire language), with IDVARVAL holding values such as "BPI" and "ADAS-COG". [Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/examples.md -- Example 2]

CDISC Notes: "ARMCD is limited to 20 characters and does not have special character restrictions. The maximum length of ARMCD is longer than that for other 'short' variables to accommodate the kind of values that are likely to be needed for crossover trials. For example, if ARMCD values for a 7-period crossover were constructed using 2-character abbreviations for each treatment and separating hyphens, the length of ARMCD values would be 20." [Source: domains/TA/spec.md -- ARMCD]

Note the contrast with the same-named variable in other domains: in DM, ARMCD is a **Record Qualifier / Exp** [Source: domains/DM/spec.md -- ARMCD], and in TV it is likewise **Record Qualifier / Exp** [Source: domains/TV/spec.md -- ARMCD]. ARMCD appears in 3 domains: DM, TA, TV [Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md -- §一 通用变量: ARMCD]. TA is the source of truth for arm codes: with the exception of multistage arm-assignment trials, DM.ARMCD/ACTARMCD must be populated with ARMCD values from the TA dataset, and the one-to-one ARM↔ARMCD relationship in TA must be preserved in DM [Source: domains/DM/assumptions.md -- item_4].

## ETCD

The retrieved context does **not** include the TA specification row for ETCD, so I cannot give you its authoritative Label, Type, Role, Core, or CDISC Notes. What the available context supports:

- The Trial Design Model divides each arm (a planned path through the trial covering the entire time of the trial) into **study cells**, one per epoch, and elements are the building blocks referenced by the Trial Elements (TE) dataset [Source: domains/TA/assumptions.md -- overview].
- ETCD functions as the short code for an element and is paired one-to-one with the descriptive ELEMENT name; this pairing is visible in the Subject Elements (SE) data, e.g. ETCD "SCRN"/ELEMENT "Screen", ETCD "DBA"/ELEMENT "Treatment A", ETCD "OA"/ELEMENT "Open Drug A", ETCD "RSC"/ELEMENT "Rescue" [Source: domains/DM/examples.md -- Example 3].

For the definitive ETCD attributes in TA (and its ordering/Core status), read `domains/TA/spec.md` in full and `domains/TE/spec.md` for the element definitions it references.
